title: app-shell geometry e2e assertions stale since density removal (3da7dec)
description:
Two assertions in web/e2e/app-shell-rebuild.spec.ts have been failing since 3da7dec baked the 0.9 spacing factor into Tailwind's --spacing base.

FAILING
- e2e/app-shell-rebuild.spec.ts:56  top bar height  expected 56, got 50
- e2e/app-shell-rebuild.spec.ts:217 nav row height  expected 42, got 38

CAUSE
Before 3da7dec, --density defaulted to 1, so --spacing was 0.25rem and h-14 computed to exactly 56px. 3da7dec removed the density knob and baked 0.9 in (--spacing: calc(0.25rem * 0.9)). Every spacing-derived dimension is now 0.9x:
- top-bar.tsx uses h-14  -> 0.9 * 56 = 50.4 -> 50
- sidebar-nav.tsx nav rows use py-2.5 + leading-[normal] -> 38

Both ratios are 0.893 / 0.905, i.e. the 0.9 factor.

DECISION NEEDED - these are prototype-absolute values (the prototype specifies a 56px top bar and 42px nav rows), so there are two defensible fixes:
a) The shell chrome is exempt from the 0.9 content scale: pin top-bar to h-[56px] and nav rows to a fixed height, keeping the prototype geometry. Tests stay as-is.
b) The whole shell is legitimately 0.9-scaled (this is what the user has been looking at, since ns-density=compact was what shipped): update the expectations to 50 and 38.

Not decided here because it is a design call, not a test-hygiene call.

VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING: reproduced at clean HEAD (f14057e) with the design-system guide changes stashed - 12 passed, same 2 failed.
close_reason: Resolved option (b) per user decision 2026-07-26: the 0.9-scaled shell is correct because it is what shipped. Updated the two e2e expectations to the scaled figures (56->50, 42->38) in web/e2e/app-shell-rebuild.spec.ts, with comments recording WHY the scaled value is the intended one so the next reader does not 'fix' it back. Also corrected three stale source comments that still asserted the unscaled prototype figures (app-shell.tsx and top-bar.tsx said 56px, sidebar-nav.tsx said ~42px) - those comments were the same trap that produced this bead. Verified: full playwright 275 passed (was 273 passed / 2 failed), vitest 2430 passed, oxlint and tsc clean.

title: Investigate: is weighted contracted-hours attainable-max a provably safe 28th Tier-1 check?
description:
BLOCKS TICKETING s30. Surfaced by cold critique 2026-07-27 (reviews/two-tier-revision-critique), which found an earlier scope claim overstated.

THE GAP: catalogue check 9 ('direct unit single-shift count whose +inf predicate is impossible over x in [0,n]') fires only on UNIT coefficients. Check 10 covers uniform-coefficient CONGRUENCE (T mod c != 0), not attainable-max. Check 12 is two unit shifts with summed minima > #dates. So 'contracted to 160h but this window cannot hold it' is detected when every shift is one unit, and NOT when shift durations vary - which is the ordinary case for contracted hours, and exactly the scenario the ortools research raised.

THE QUESTION: is a WEIGHTED attainable-max check provably zero-false-positive? max_x is already computed at core/nurse_scheduling/preference_types.py:463-480, so the arithmetic is cheap. The risk is whether bounding it needs packing reasoning at the margins (varying durations + leave pins + qualification exclusions), which is precisely the class the catalogue's final pruning cut.

METHOD: match how the catalogue was built - run the actual CP-SAT scheduler as an oracle on candidate shapes. A shape that returns OPTIMAL kills the check. Do NOT accept a reasoning-only argument.

OUTCOMES: (a) provably safe -> a legitimate 28th check, add to the catalogue with its precondition; (b) needs packing -> stays out, firewall holds, record it in the NEEDS-SOLVER list so it is not re-proposed a third time.

DO NOT add on plausibility. Every one of the 27 was CP-SAT-verified; the zero-false-positive guarantee is the whole value of Tier 1 and one false alarm costs more trust than this check can earn.
acceptance_criteria: A documented verdict backed by actual CP-SAT runs on candidate shapes, plus a catalogue update either adding the check with its precondition or recording it under NEEDS-SOLVER.
close_reason:
VERDICT: PROVABLY SAFE. Added to the catalogue as G7; the v1 set is now 28.

THE CHECK. Hard (.inf) shift count with a LOWER-BOUND predicate is infeasible when:
  'x >= T' or 'x = T':  T  >  len(expanded countDates) * max(coefficients)
  'x > T':              T >=  len(expanded countDates) * max(coefficients)

SOUNDNESS (structural, verified in code not inferred). scheduler.py enforces exactly one day-state per person-day UNCONDITIONALLY: offs[(d,p)] + sum_s shifts[(d,s,p)] + leaves[(d,p)] == 1, in a plain per-day/per-person loop with no guard. Separately, 'at most one shift per day' is a REQUIRED preference - the loader raises 'Missing required preferences' without it. So each day contributes at most max(coeff) to x, giving x <= len(c_ds) * max(coeff), which is exactly the model's own max_x at preference_types.py:478. A lower-bound target above that is unsatisfiable by construction.

TWO HAZARDS CLOSED BY BUILD-TIME VALIDATION, not by detector logic:
- negative/zero coefficients impossible - 'Shift count coefficient for N must be at least 1'
- double-counting impossible - 'Duplicate shift count coefficient for D' rejects overlapping entries
If either validation is relaxed, G7 must be re-verified.

ORACLE: 22 scenarios through the real nurse_scheduling.schedule() on pinned ortools==9.15.6755. Unit and weighted forms; exact boundary (T == max_x solved OPTIMAL in every variant, so the check must fire only strictly above); half-hour contracted shapes over 28 days; 'x = T' and 'x > T' arms; multi-pair Range ['x >= T','x <= T']; OFF and ALL in countShiftTypes; duplicate shift entries; date-group and person-group expansion; a staffing cap competing with the count. Upper-bound predicates ('x <= T', 'x < T') solved as required - they must NEVER fire. Finite weight solved - soft must never be treated as a conflict. ZERO VIOLATIONS: no shape solved where the rule predicted infeasible.

HONEST LIMIT - do not oversell this. max_x assumes the longest shift is workable on EVERY date, so it ignores leave pinning (G4), staffing caps and successions. It is loose and will miss most genuinely-tight windows: verified case {D:2, LEAVE:10} over 6 dates at T=59 is truly INFEASIBLE (only 12 reachable) but sits under max_x=60 and stays silent. For realistic contracted hours it will rarely fire - 160h over 28 days is nowhere near a 12h/day ceiling. Its real value is catching GROSS MIS-ENTRY, above all unit confusion (a target typed in minutes, or a monthly figure against a fortnightly roster). Worth shipping for that; not contracted-hours feasibility checking.

ALSO SETTLED: horizon-wide 'aggregate demand vs supply' - proposed twice - is now recorded in the catalogue's NEEDS-SOLVER list so it stops being re-proposed. It is not in v1, not Dropped, not Rejected.

Artifacts updated: verified-conflict-catalogue (G7 section + set count + NEEDS-SOLVER entry), path-to-feasibility-two-tier (Resolved section, correction table, counts), rule-conflict-validation flow (counts).

title: Tier 1: Deterministic client-side feasibility checks (keyless, always on)
description:
Own initiative, sequenced IN PARALLEL with the roster viewer (cjr) and independent of the AI assistant panel (t34). Decided 2026-07-27.

SCOPE = the existing solver-verified 27-check catalogue, UNCHANGED. Pure client-side arithmetic/set checks over data the frontend already holds. No LLM, no BYO key, no backend, no CP-SAT at runtime. Always on - this is the keyless layer that makes 'path to feasibility' real rather than a placeholder (memory: ai-features-optional-byo-key).

CORRECTION (2026-07-27): an earlier version of this bead listed four checks from ortools research as if they were new scope. They are NOT. Mapped against the catalogue: (1) pairwise hard-pin contradiction scan = already G1/G6/check-26; (2) per-date coverage vs headcount = checks 4/5 in singleton form, while the GENERAL form ('required > staff/qualified') is on the catalogue's Rejected must-NOT-warn list because a coefficient >1 lets one nurse supply several units; (3) contracted hours vs attainable max = checks 9/12, and the research summary omits red-team precondition #9 (test the predicate's satisfiable set, not raw 0..U membership); (4) aggregate demand vs supply = checks 7/13, EXPLICITLY DROPPED in final pruning because CP-SAT returned OPTIMAL on them. Do not implement (4). Do not implement the general form of (2).

The research's real contribution is confirming this layer needs no backend and no solver - which is what lets it ship in parallel and stay keyless.

RUNS ON BOTH SIDES OF THE RUN (new): pre-submit warn (consolidated panel, fix-first) AND replay after an infeasible run. Previously pre-run only.

FIREWALL RULE (load-bearing): fires only on fully-expanded, concrete, single-target, literal rules. Precision over recall by construction. The catalogue reached 27 by running CP-SAT as an oracle and cutting everything that came back feasible. One false alarm costs more trust than a check can earn back.
design:
Product behavior is ALREADY SPECIFIED and tech-plan-ready - do not re-plan it:
- flows/rule-conflict-validation/index.md (the flow; warning hierarchy, fix-first override, shared conflict model, deep-link contract, a11y)
- flows/rule-conflict-validation/verified-conflict-catalogue/index.md (the 27 checks + rejected/dropped lists + detectability notes)
- flows/rule-conflict-validation/behavioral-matrix/index.md (per-surface x per-family behavior)
Only computation remains open: re-evaluation scheduling/debounce, incremental vs full recompute, the detector module, per-surface wiring.

PUBLISHES THE SHARED CONFLICT MODEL consumed by Tier 2 (3d4): { what conflicts, participating refs, plain reason, suggested fix(es), links per participant }. Cross-initiative contract, not an internal type - a later change breaks a separate initiative.

Detectability: most checks need only frontend state. Check 20 needs Person.history (on the client); checks 4/5/8/G1 need hard-request leave/off pin data. None require the solver.

NOT blocked on l3m. Research found a true CP-SAT unsat core is a trap: needs a second objective-free solve (with a real objective the core returns ALL assumptions), forces single-threading, weakens presolve, returns empty when the infeasibility is outside the gated set, and omits the structural co-conspirators. l3m is superseded as specified; if backend evidence is revived it should be elastic/slack re-solve, not IIS.

Governed by decisions/path-to-feasibility-two-tier (revised 2026-07-27).
acceptance_criteria: With AI disabled and no API key present, a scenario matching any of the 27 catalogue checks is flagged before submit AND re-surfaced after an infeasible run, naming the concrete nurse/date/shift/rule participants in plain language. Zero false positives: no warning fires on any shape in the catalogue's Rejected or Dropped lists. When Tier 1 finds nothing and the run is still infeasible, the copy says so plainly and does not imply a backstop exists.
notes:
Two-tier decision revised 2026-07-27; this bead's scope corrected to the 27-check catalogue.
FLOW REVISED 2026-07-27: rule-conflict-validation now specifies THREE surfaces. New surface 3 = post-infeasible replay (flow state D), keyless and always on, rendered inside the Optimize Infeasible panel below the solver verdict.

Key product rules for the replay:
- Runs against the SUBMITTED REVISION, not current editor state. If unavailable, say so and offer a re-check of current state as an explicitly different thing - never silently substitute.
- Same 27 checks, NO new detection power. Its job is attribution + scope honesty at the moment of failure, not investigation. Copy must not imply the app analysed the failure.
- Never presented as the solver's reason (solver returns only INFEASIBLE + infeasibility_proven). Labelled as our own check, offered as the LIKELY cause. This is what keeps it distinct from the prototype's rejected 'tightest conflicts' list.
- State D1 (findings): lead with attribution, not a repeat of the warning; if the user overrode these exact conflicts say so once, factual not scolding. Action is Adjust rules, NOT fix-first framing (the run already happened).
- State D2 (nothing found): must not read as reassurance, must not read as app failure, must not imply anyone is looking further.
- When AI is on, the Tier-2 offer sits BELOW the replay - free/certain before paid/heuristic.

OPEN FOR TECH-PLAN (check before ticketing): does the existing submission session already retain the submitted revision, or is a minimal snapshot needed? The roster viewer's cjr.2.2 captures something similar - do not build two mechanisms, but do NOT give s30 a dependency on cjr.
COLD CRITIQUE APPLIED 2026-07-27 (reviews/two-tier-revision-critique). Three corrections to THIS bead's earlier notes:

1. MECHANISM CHANGED - replay carries findings forward, does NOT retain a scenario snapshot. Verified: the submission session record is closed-key and hasExactKeys-validated (web/lib/optimize/session-transaction.ts:55-84, allowlist :858-871) and does NOT retain the scenario; T16q forbids a scenario backup or second safety journal. Persisting the FINDING SET (which already exists at submit) is equivalent to persisting the input and recomputing, and far cheaper. This is what keeps s30 free of any dependency on cjr.2.2. Open for tech-plan: the additive versioned field + a finding-set size cap (a truncated set must not read as complete).

2. MY EARLIER MAPPING WAS WRONG on 'aggregate demand vs supply'. It is NOT checks 7/13 (those are member-vs-aggregate-TERM and count-vs-staffing ALIGNMENT). Horizon-wide demand-vs-supply is in none of the 27, the Dropped list, or the Rejected list - its home is NEEDS-SOLVER. It still stays OUT, but on the firewall rule + design-correction-#1 (weighted capacity), not on a pruning result. Also overstated: check 26 is SOLE-preceptor only, not 'no available preceptor' generally.

3. POSSIBLE REAL GAP - weighted contracted-hours attainable-max. Check 9 is UNIT-coefficient only; check 10 covers uniform-coefficient congruence, not attainable-max. So '160h contracted but the window cannot hold it' is undetected when shift durations vary - the ordinary contracted-hours case. INVESTIGATE BEFORE TICKETING: is a weighted attainable-max check provably zero-false-positive? max_x already computed at preference_types.py:463-480. If provably safe it is a legitimate 28th check; if it needs packing reasoning at the margins it stays out. DO NOT add on plausibility - every catalogue member was CP-SAT-verified.

Also noted by the critique, not yet actioned: the Optimize panel's 'Try again' sits next to a PROOF of infeasibility and implies further looking; resubmit re-derives from the LIVE store (optimize-and-export-screen.tsx:230). And 'verdict: infeasibility_proven' is rendered in a monospace data box but is a hardcoded literal at core/nurse_scheduling/server/jobs/runner.py:97 - a constant presented as solver data.
qbc RESOLVED 2026-07-27: scope is now the 28-check catalogue. G7 (weighted attainable-max) added and CP-SAT-verified. Fires when a HARD count with a lower-bound predicate has T > len(expanded countDates) * max(coefficients). Preconditions: hard weight only; lower-bound predicates only ('x <= T'/'x < T' must NEVER fire); non-empty person AND date expansion. Coefficients >= 1 and non-overlapping are guaranteed by build-time validation - if either is relaxed, re-verify G7. Loose bound by design: its real value is catching unit-confusion mis-entry, not tight-window detection. s30 is unblocked and ready to brief/ticket.
EPIC BRIEF DRAFTED 2026-07-28: .traycer/epics/8b2235d5-8943-4f6d-a61e-3b671836217a/artifacts/tier-1-feasibility-checks/index.md

Standalone initiative dir (mirrors in-app-roster-viewer). Downstream artifacts are NOT moved - the brief links to them where they live under app-prototype-fidelity-audit/ (flow, verified catalogue, behavioral matrix, two-tier decision), so no inbound links break.

Brief is ORIENTATION ONLY and says so - product behaviour and the check inventory are already settled and tech-plan-ready elsewhere. It should not be treated as the specification.

Framing recorded: the solver returns bare INFEASIBLE with no reasons, so a user is told their roster is impossible and left to guess. Some of those failures are pure arithmetic the frontend can already spot. This closes that gap where certainty is achievable and stays silent everywhere else.

Why it matters now: AI is off by default and needs a user key, so for the majority who never enable it this is the ENTIRE safety net - it must never depend on the optional tier. And it has no dependencies and needs no backend, so it is the one post-parity initiative that can start immediately.

Load-bearing constraints in the brief: zero false positives by construction (firewall rule); every catalogue member CP-SAT-verified and any future addition must clear the same committed harness bar; must stay useful with AI off forever; the shared conflict model is a cross-initiative published contract consumed by 3d4.

Remaining for tech plan is computation only: re-evaluation scheduling, incremental vs full recompute, detector module, per-surface wiring, and where the carried finding set is stored.
TECH PLAN DRAFTED 2026-07-28: artifacts/tier-1-feasibility-checks/tech-plan/index.md

GOVERNING DECISION: mirror web/lib/scenario/leave-guard/ - an already-shipped, tested detector solving a structurally identical problem. Nothing is invented. It answers all four hard points: one pure module owns policy; a FAIL-CLOSED resolution context keeps backend fidelity; the detector is IDENTITY-FREE with an adapter joining findings to uid positionally within one snapshot; and consumers 'must adapt into the structural input rather than growing their own approximation' (the anti-drift rule is already convention there).

1. DETECTOR - new dir web/lib/scenario/conflicts/ with detector.ts / resolution.ts / adapters.ts / conflict-model.ts. Input is a narrow structural snapshot of UI TYPES, not the canonical document: canonical deliberately strips uid ('neither the projection nor this type ever reads a card uid') and every finding must link to an editable participant. Enablement passed in, never re-derived.
   REUSE, DO NOT REIMPLEMENT: generateDateIds (lib/dates/date-id.ts), expandDateRefs + expandShiftTypeRefs (lib/rules/expansion.ts), sameRef exact identity (lib/cascade/reference-tree.ts). A second expansion implementation that drifts turns a CERTAIN finding into a false positive - the one failure this initiative cannot absorb.
   TWO INVARIANTS: fail-closed (unresolvable selector suppresses the check); and the firewall rule enforced as an explicit per-check precondition guard, not implied by the arithmetic.

2. CONFLICT MODEL - published cross-initiative contract consumed by 3d4. participants is PLURAL (a conflict is a relationship, not one rule's error). reason is a structured template + values, never a formatted string, because the 28 messages need pluralisation/localised dates/long-name handling and Tier 2 must re-render the same finding.

3. IDENTITY - index in, uid out. Adapters return byCardUid / byRequestCell maps. A positional index must NEVER be persisted or rejoined after the array reorders (leave-guard states this explicitly). Root-cause grouping lives in the report, not the UI, since the flow counts fixable groups.

4. RE-EVALUATION - full recompute over a snapshot; narrow Pick<> slice + useMemo per components/home/scenario-summary.ts (also the answer to b8z). ONE evaluation shared by all consumers - two could disagree and the flow makes the panel authoritative. BUDGET vs ~87 people x 31 days: author-time <= 16ms (one frame), panel <= 150ms on demand. Debounce only if breached; incremental explicitly OUT until then. No pre-emptive debounce - an unmeasured interval is a guess.

5. PER-SURFACE WIRING - inline reads byCardUid/byRequestCell (own kind only); panel reads groups; replay reads the carried set; health indicator reads all.length. Non-rule screens get NO per-field marker.

6. CARRIED SET - ephemeral run state, not durable. Not the submission record: closed-key + hasExactKeys means a schema bump, and T16q forbids a scenario backup or second safety journal. The flow's no-findings-carried fallback already exists, so a reload degrades into a DESIGNED state. Cap the set and render truncation as explicitly truncated.

7. TESTING - catalogue membership stays oracle-gated (core/tests/catalogue_oracle.py); detector unit tests cover the frontend half the oracle cannot; the Rejected and NEEDS-SOLVER lists get NEGATIVE tests asserting silence, which is what stops a measured false positive being reintroduced.

OUT OF SCOPE: any core/ change; consolidating the five duplicated expandDateRange copies (canonical generateDateIds already exists - file separately, touches 5 shipped components); incremental recompute; Tier 2 and elastic re-solve.
TECH PLAN CRITIQUED + CORRECTED 2026-07-28. Critique: artifacts/tier-1-feasibility-checks/tech-plan/critique/index.md.

CENTRAL BET SURVIVED: mirroring leave-guard is structurally sound. The cross-family identity worry did NOT materialise - ConflictParticipant carries cardKind alongside index, so a finding naming two different card kinds joins to two uids cleanly.

B1 (BLOCKING) - MY PLAN CITED THE WRONG HELPER FAMILY, contradicting its own fail-closed invariant. lib/rules/expansion.ts is FAIL-OPEN: expandDateRefs adds unrecognised tokens 'verbatim as a concrete date id', expandShiftTypeRefs silently drops unknowns, neither returns a resolved/unresolved signal, both String()-coerce so 1 and '1' collapse, and there is NO people resolver there at all. Meanwhile lib/scenario/leave-guard/resolution.ts ALREADY IS what the plan described wanting: Resolution<T> = {resolved:true;values}|{resolved:false} (an explicit unresolved signal), buildPeopleIndexMap/resolvePeopleSelector, resolveShiftTypeSelector, buildDateIndexMap/resolveDateSelector, TypedMapKey = number|string. FIX APPLIED: promote leave-guard/resolution.ts to lib/scenario/resolution/, shared by leave-guard/ and conflicts/. ROOT CAUSE OF MY ERROR: lib/rules/expansion.ts:1-15 declares itself 'the SHARED FOUNDATION consumed by ... the Tier-1 conflict detector' - a stale forward-reference that must be corrected or it will mislead the implementer too.

B2 (BLOCKING) - ConflictReport could not represent 'Checks unavailable', which the behavioral matrix requires and says must not imply a clean scenario. all.length===0 meant both clean and crashed. FIXED: added status: 'checked'|'unavailable'|'not-ready'; the health indicator reads status FIRST.

B3 (BLOCKING) - ephemeral storage landed in a real gap: resetRun/resetRunView/resetEphemeral each clear EXPLICIT KEY LISTS, so a new sibling key is cleared by none of them and scenario A's findings would survive a Load into scenario B; placing it inside runView gets wiped by every setRunView. FIXED: use the store's existing runGeneration - stamp the carried set, treat a generation mismatch as not-carried. Staleness becomes structurally impossible.

C1 - my rationale for rejecting the submission record was FACTUALLY WRONG: only the PROVISIONAL variant uses hasExactKeys; the ACTIVE variant uses hasAllowedKeys and already carries an additive optional (lastCursor). Conclusion (ephemeral) stands but on corrected grounds: sessionStorage is per-tab and torn down anyway. Now also prices the consequence - every recovered session takes the degraded path, so that path must read as normal, not as an error.

G3 - PERFORMANCE MEASURED AND THE BUDGET HOLDS: context build 0.108ms, resolvePeople('ALL') 3.5us, 181 cards x resolution triple ~0.95ms. BUT only under a resolve-once-and-share invariant the plan never stated - naive per-check re-resolution is 5.7ms and a naive per-cell request scan 9.7ms, together ~15.4ms, consuming the whole frame before any check runs. FIXED: resolve-once is now stated as load-bearing, not an optimisation.

G5 - grouping was asserted, never defined ('biggest invention risk'). FIXED with a definition: two findings group when their participant sets overlap on an editable participant, unioned transitively; panel count is groups.length, never all.length.

C2 - the 'narrow slice' is effectively the whole scenario slice, so it does NOT by itself answer b8z. FIXED: now says so, and states what actually prevents re-render storms (consumers subscribe to their slice of the REPORT, not the report object).

C3 - only G7 has a committed oracle test; the other 27 have NO regression gate. FIXED: backfilling oracle cases for all 27 is now IN SCOPE, not optional.

G1 - typed request-cell keys (concatenation collapses 1 vs '1'); request participants must carry their selector or G6 cannot name its two sides. G2 - index-in/refs-out asymmetry made explicit; nothing downstream may map a ref back to an index.

ALSO: the artifact contained ONE NUL BYTE from my own '\0' key-separator notation, which made it a binary file and broke grep/text tooling. Stripped; file is valid UTF-8 again.
SECOND TECH-PLAN CRITIQUE APPLIED 2026-07-28. Artifact: tech-plan/critique-2/index.md. Its closing observation was accurate and worth keeping: 'every finding about the plan's INPUTS was fixed properly; every finding about its published OUTPUT CONTRACT was answered with a paragraph describing the problem.' This round changed types, not prose.

BLOCKER 1 - THE CARRIED SET COULD NOT LEGALLY EXIST. Section 3 forbade persisting a positional index; section 6 persisted exactly that, because ConflictParticipant was index-based, so 'all' and 'groups' inherited it and only byCardUid was ever joined. Consequences: the replay would rejoin indices against a possibly-reordered array, and the panel (which consumes groups) could not deep-link at all. FIXED IN THE TYPE: participants now carry { cardKind, uid }, never an index; findConflicts joins before returning; index is confined to the detector's internal type.

BLOCKER 2 - TRANSITIVE GROUPING FALSIFIED ITS OWN JUSTIFICATION. The rationale was 'editing one participant clears them together', which transitivity breaks in one hop (A~B, B~C, but editing A does not clear C). Modelled against real checks, a chain 5 -> 8 -> G1 -> 14 -> 11 merges into one group, and it is monotone the WRONG WAY: broad ALL-selector cards are participation hubs, so the count trends to 1 exactly when the scenario has the most problems. It would render the flow's own wireframe ('2 conflicts: AM understaffed + Priya double-booked') as '1 conflict', and it contradicted the flow's 'dedupe equivalent pairs'. FIXED: group on participant-set EQUALITY, not overlap. Twelve findings of the same shape across twelve dates = one group with twelve instances; two different problems stay two groups even when they share a card.

BLOCKER 3 - 'ALREADY GENERIC' WAS HALF RIGHT. The leave-coupling claim HELD (verified: no LEAVE_SID, no count-card shape, ResolutionContextInput is pure scenario domain, 4 call sites) so the promotion is genuinely cheap. But COVERAGE fails two ways, now priced into the plan as required work: (a) the resolvers take FLAT selectors only, while successions/affinities/coverings/requirements carry Nested*RefList (Array<T|T[]>) - roughly 18 of 28 checks; reuse lib/cascade/reference-tree.ts's RefTree recursion rather than writing a second one. (b) there is NO index->shift-type inverse, and shifts[i] is an INVALID inverse because the index space includes OFF_SID=-1 and LEAVE_SID=-2 - precisely the day-states G3/G4 reason about.

ALSO FIXED: status is now two values, not three - 'not-ready' duplicated the shipped deriveOptimizeReadiness (web/lib/optimize/optimize-readiness.ts), a third representation of Setup required inside a cross-initiative contract. And section 4 ('one evaluation') contradicted section 5 ('a final evaluation runs at submit'); reconciled as one evaluation PER REVISION, with submission as a FRESHNESS BARRIER against the same saved revision, never an independent second opinion that could disagree with the panel.

ORACLE PREMISE WAS FALSE - the most important correction. The plan claimed backfilling 27 oracle cases would stop an implementation mis-encoding a check. It would not: the Python oracle asserts a PYTHON PREDICATE against CP-SAT and never executes the TS detector, so it validates the CATALOGUE, not the CODE. Two distinct gates are now named separately, connected by a SHARED FIXTURE CORPUS so the scenario CP-SAT proved infeasible is literally the scenario the detector is asserted to fire on. Backfill split out to bead cqr (~5 new builders, 27 predicates, several hundred shapes) rather than absorbed silently here.

STILL OPEN from round 1, not addressed by either pass: G2 (index->ref inverse direction) and G4 (no module owns the 28 message templates).
TICKETS DRAFTED 2026-07-28: artifacts/tier-1-feasibility-checks/tickets/ - index + 9 tickets (T1-T9).

BOTH OPEN GAPS RESOLVED BY THE BREAKDOWN, not deferred:
G2 (nobody owned the index->ref inverse) -> T1. All three inverses (people, dates, shift types) live in the RESOLUTION MODULE, which already owns the forward direction and therefore the index space. Adapters call them, never rebuild them. Two traps named in the ticket: shifts[i] is invalid because the index space includes OFF_SID=-1/LEAVE_SID=-2; and the date inverse must produce the span-compressed id form current for the committed range or every deep-link points at nothing.
G4 (no module owned the 28 templates) -> T3. A dedicated content module owns all 28 structured templates, pluralisation, localised dates, long-name handling and the glossary, mirroring leave-guard's warning-format.ts. Split out as its own ticket because it is real content work, and because inline templates in React would make them unreusable by Tier 2 - which defeats the shared conflict model.

SEQUENCE: T1 resolution foundation -> T2 model+pipeline+grouping (one check, G1, proves it end to end; also establishes the shared fixture format) -> T4/T5/T6 check families in parallel -> T7 panel + health indicator -> T8 inline markers -> T9 replay. T3 (content) depends only on the catalogue so it runs in PARALLEL with T1/T2; T7 and T9 depend on it.

T7 BEFORE T8 DELIBERATELY: the panel is authoritative, so it must exist before inline markers have to agree with it.

Each ticket carries the traps that would otherwise be rediscovered: T4 - coefficients break headcount maths (raw required>staff is on the Rejected list), preferred is a HARD upper bound, staffing/coverings are hard at ANY weight. T5 - G7 already has 24 committed oracle cases to reuse; check 9 must test the predicate's SATISFIABLE SET not raw 0..U; LEAVE is a fixed input. T6 - needs T1's nested-ref support (affinities/coverings are one level deep, imports arbitrary); a forbidden succession forbids the whole CONJUNCTION, not each state. T9 - stamp with runGeneration, since the three reset paths use explicit key lists and a sibling key would be cleared by none.

OUT OF SCOPE FOR ALL TICKETS: any core/ change; oracle backfill for the other 27 checks (bead cqr); expandDateRange consolidation (bead l0o); incremental recomputation.

QUICK-PAINT CRITIQUE RECONCILED 2026-07-29 in the source tech-plan artifact (tier-1-feasibility-checks/tech-plan §4). The recovered prior plan/critique was found under app-prototype-fidelity-audit artifacts, so the missing-plan blocker is closed. Settled lifecycle: hot.paint stages crossed cells only; no detector run during drag; surfaces mark the retained report "Changes not yet checked"; cancel/empty gesture requires no evaluation; pointer-up performs one atomic setReqData and exactly one immediate full evaluation; submit remains a synchronous un-debounced freshness barrier over the durable snapshot. Normalize reqData once per evaluation; request-only cross-revision caching is optional and must not ignore group/context changes. T1 scope is unchanged and remains unstarted.

title: Flaky e2e: optimize-screen 'no horizontal overflow at mobile'
description:
e2e/optimize-screen.spec.ts:110 "has no horizontal overflow at mobile" fails intermittently. Measured with --repeat-each=8 against production builds:

  at 54e0ed9 (parent, BEFORE the layout-ladder commit):  1 of 8 failed
  at 4f03f60 (HEAD, after it):                           2 of 8 failed

Statistically indistinguishable, so it PREDATES 4f03f60 and is not a bmw.6 regression. Full-suite runs pass (278/278) more often than not, which is why it survived unnoticed.

When it fails the number is always the same: documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth = 475 at a 375px viewport. A stable value from an unstable moment points at a transient pre-settle layout rather than random noise — the page is measured after `toBeVisible` on the fixture root but evidently before something finishes sizing. The fixture renders the running state including the progress chart, which measures its container, so chart/ResizeObserver settling is the first place to look.

Probing the SAME production build out-of-band could not reproduce it: a direct Playwright probe replicating the spec exactly (Desktop Chrome device, setViewportSize(375x812), goto, waitForSelector) reports scrollWidth - clientWidth = 0 and ZERO elements past the viewport edge, repeatedly. It only misbehaves under the suite's parallel workers, which supports a timing/settling cause over a layout one.

RULED OUT: a missing `w-full` on the screen root. `mx-auto flex w-full max-w-6xl flex-col gap-6 px-5 py-8` became `flex flex-col gap-6` in bmw.6, and /optimize-screen-fixture lives outside the (app) route group (so no AppShell container) and lays children out as a flex column — a plausible max-content story. Tested: adding `w-full` back still fails 2 of 8. Not the cause; the change was reverted rather than left in on a wrong diagnosis.
design: Fix direction, not chosen: make the assertion wait for a settled layout rather than a visible root — e.g. poll scrollWidth until stable across two frames, or await the chart's own readiness signal before measuring. Prefer that over widening the tolerance, which would blind the test to the real overflow it is there to catch. Whoever takes it should first capture WHAT is wide at the failing moment (the out-of-band probe finds nothing, so the capture has to happen inside the failing run — an evaluate on failure, or a trace).
acceptance_criteria: e2e/optimize-screen.spec.ts passes --repeat-each=20 with zero failures, and still fails when a genuine horizontal overflow is introduced at mobile.
notes:
INDEPENDENT DATA POINT 2026-07-26 (second agent, separate run). Supports the load/settling hypothesis over a layout cause.

Run A — full suite against the WORKTREE while a second production build + suite were running concurrently on the same 32-core host (two 'next build' processes contending):
  13 failed / 258 passed / 7 did not run
  failures: app-shell.spec x5, counts.spec x6, mode-aware-shell.spec x1, optimize-screen.spec 'has no horizontal overflow at mobile' x1

Run B — the same optimize-screen.spec alone, no contention, fresh production build:
  7 passed, including 'has no horizontal overflow at mobile'

Run C — full suite against HEAD (4f03f60), no contention:
  278 passed, 0 failed — the overflow test among them

So the overflow test is not the only thing that goes red under load; app-shell and counts specs did too, and all of them pass clean. That is a broader signal than one flaky measurement: the failures track HOST CONTENTION, not the diff. Worth checking whether the chart container's measurement is simply racing first paint under starved CPU, and whether the suite needs an explicit settle before measuring scrollWidth rather than a tighter worker cap.

Note run A was against the worktree (five streams incl. the uncommitted card-editor work), runs B and C against committed trees, so run A is not a clean comparison for anything but the contention observation.
ROOT CAUSE FOUND, and it was not where either earlier guess pointed. Captured by instrumenting the assertion itself and running --repeat-each=12: 3 failures, all byte-identical.

    overflow 475, scrollWidth 850, clientWidth 375
    readyState complete, fonts loaded, CSS applied (root max-width 1152px, padding 20px)
    offender: <svg data-testid="progress-chart-score-panel"> w=800 right=850, plus 31 child nodes

components/optimize/progress-chart/progress-chart.tsx: DEFAULT_CONTAINER_WIDTH = 800 is held in useState until a ResizeObserver effect reports the real container width, and ProgressPanel renders <svg width={containerWidth}>. So the chart paints at 800px before that callback fires. At a 375px viewport 800px + the 20px page padding lands the SVG right edge at 850 — the 475px overflow exactly, every time. Whether the assertion wins the race against the observer decided pass or fail. Nothing to do with CSS, hydration, or the missing w-full I chased earlier.

FIX (e2e/optimize-screen.spec.ts): replaced the single measurement with expect.poll on scrollWidth - clientWidth. A visible root is not a settled layout; polling measures the settled one. Deliberately NOT a widened tolerance, which would have blinded the test to the overflow it exists to catch.

VERIFIED both ways, in a scratch worktree isolated from other agents in-flight edits:
- --repeat-each=20 -> 140 passed, 0 failed (was 1-2 in 8).
- Teeth intact: injecting a deliberate 1400px-wide element into the fixture fails BOTH mobile and desktop, after the poll timeout rather than instantly.

REAL BEHAVIOUR THIS EXPOSES, not fixed here: the transient is genuine, not a test artifact. On an actual 375px device the chart paints at 800px on first render and the page really does overflow horizontally until the ResizeObserver fires. Filed separately.
SWEEP FOR SIBLINGS (asked after the fix): every geometry measurement in the e2e suite audited, then stress-tested. NO other spec carries this race. No code changed.

Inventory — 11 specs measure geometry (scrollWidth/clientWidth/offsetWidth/getBoundingClientRect/boundingBox). Three shapes, only one of which can race:

1. Measure-and-use inside ONE synchronous evaluate — the drag simulations in affinities, counts, requirements, successions read a target card rect and dispatch drop events in the same evaluate. Nothing can settle between read and use. Not exposed.
2. Measurement AFTER an interaction — optimize-progress-chart reads scorePanel.boundingBox() in six places to derive hover/tap coordinates, which is the same component that caused 02h. It is protected, but INCIDENTALLY: the preceding fixture-dataset click costs an actionability check and a round trip, which is enough for the ResizeObserver to fire. Measured directly, mirroring the spec: first read = settled width = 948px in 12 of 12 runs, never the 800 fallback. Same for shift-requests, which scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()s before reading cell boxes.
3. Static chrome — app-shell-rebuild (rail, nav rows, drawer), dates (roster vs calendar), design-system (skeleton vs card). Nothing resizes post-paint.

02h was the only case of shape 4: measure immediately after a bare toBeVisible(), with no interaction in between, on a component that resizes after first paint.

STRESS EVIDENCE (isolated worktree at 8075e8c, production build):
  full suite --repeat-each=3   -> 834 passed, 0 failed
  the six geometry specs --repeat-each=12 -> 864 passed, 0 failed

Deliberately did NOT add polls prophylactically. Nothing here is proven broken, the protection that exists is real, and blanket polling would cost suite time while hiding genuine regressions behind a timeout.

WHAT WOULD BRING IT BACK, worth knowing at review time: the protection in shape 2 is a side effect of an interaction, not an expressed intent. Deleting the dataset click from a chart test, or reordering it after the boundingBox read, silently reintroduces exactly 02h.

ADJACENT, not this bug: 12 waitForTimeout calls across 8 specs (affinities, app-shell, counts, optimize-assembled-stream, optimize-durable-stream, optimize-progress-chart, requirements, successions). Arbitrary waits rather than measurement races — covered by nursing-sheduler-5e2.
CORRECTION to the sweep note above. The line "12 waitForTimeout calls ... covered by nursing-sheduler-5e2" was wrong on both counts. 5e2 is scoped to PERSISTENCE waits specifically (its acceptance criterion is the authoritative saved-state seam), and exactly ONE of the twelve is that: app-shell.spec.ts waitForTimeout(800) after a mutate, letting auto-persist settle before a reload.

The other eleven split three ways, and only five are convertible at all:

CONVERTIBLE (5) — drag-simulation settles, 50ms between the dragstart dispatch and the drop evaluate, in affinities, counts, requirements and successions (x2: cards and pattern chips). Filed as its own bead.

NOT CONVERTIBLE (3) — negative-assertion holds, where the pause IS the assertion: app-shell re-checks the URL is still /shift-types after 300ms (guarding a delayed history.back()), and optimize-progress-chart twice re-checks the tooltip is still visible after 300ms (tap retention across a pause). You cannot poll for a non-event; replacing these with condition-based waiting would delete the thing being tested.

NOT CONVERTIBLE (3) — stream/protocol intervals where elapsed time is the point: the assembled spec waits out the backend keepalive window then asserts a real ": keepalive" chunk arrived, and waits 2s after navigation for abort teardown; the durable spec allows one controller poll/reconnect turn then asserts nothing incorrectly unlocked. Note the two assembled ones are outside the base suite anyway (testIgnore routes that spec to playwright.assembled.config.ts).

title: Layout breakpoints approximate the prototype: Tailwind's type-scale ladder stands in for a disjoint layout ladder
description:
Follow-on from the `.ns-grid3` fix in bmw.6. That was not a one-off — it is the visible
instance of a systemic mismatch.

ROOT CAUSE. The prototype has TWO breakpoint ladders:

- a TYPE-SCALE ladder at 480/768/1024/1280/1440/1920 (`Nurse Scheduling.dc.html:45-50`)
- a LAYOUT ladder at 600/620/720/760/900/1100/1200 (`:77-94`), one value per layout class

`web/app/globals.css:240-248` defines the theme's named breakpoints from the FIRST ladder
only (xs 480, sm 640, md 768, lg 1024, xl 1280, 2xl 1440, 3xl 1920, plus nav 920). None of
the layout ladder's values exist as named breakpoints, so every layout grid in the port was
approximated to the nearest type-scale stop — which is why `.ns-grid3`'s 1100px became
Tailwind's `lg` (1024px).

MISMATCHES FOUND (audit 2026-07-26):

| # | site | port | prototype | drift |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | components/save-load/save-load-workspace.tsx:86 | `lg:grid-cols-2` (1024) | `.ns-grid2` 900 | 124px LATE |
| 2 | components/optimize/optimize-and-export-screen.tsx:360 | `lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_minmax(0,1.1fr)]` (1024) | `.ns-grid2` 900, `1fr 1fr` | 124px LATE + ratio differs |
| 3 | components/home/home-guided.tsx:162 | `xl:grid-cols-3` (1280) | `.ns-wizgrid` 1200 | 80px LATE (same shape as the ns-grid3 bug) |
| 4 | components/requirements/requirement-form.tsx:265 | `md:grid-cols-2` (768) | `.ns-formgrid` 720 | 48px late |
| 5 | shift-type-grid.tsx (2 inner form rows), counts/contracted-form.tsx, entity-editor/working-time-fields.tsx | `sm:grid-cols-2` (640) | `.ns-formgrid` 720 | 80px EARLY |
| 6 | components/entity-editor/transfer-list.tsx:139 | `sm:grid-cols-2` (640) | `.ns-panes2` 600 | 40px late |

Note #4 and #5 are the SAME prototype class approximated two different ways, 128px apart.
The 640px ones matter most in practice: they force a two-column form inside narrow cards,
which is the width pressure the shift card has been fighting (see mkn, 4du).

CORRECT ALREADY, no action:
- `.ns-grid3` — both grids now `min-[1100px]:grid-cols-3` (bmw.6)
- `.ns-grid2` on Dates — hand-ported to CSS at the real 900px in components/dates/calendar.css:6-16.
  This is the one faithful case, and it is faithful BECAUSE it was written as a CSS class
  rather than approximated with a Tailwind variant. That is the precedent worth following.
- `nav:` 920px matches the prototype's sidebar pivot; `.ns-hide-sm` 768 maps to `md:` exactly
- the type-scale ladder is replicated exactly in globals.css:183-222

NOT A BREAKPOINT ISSUE, noted while auditing: `.ns-xfer` (ScreenStaff/ScreenShifts) is
`1fr auto 1fr` with a middle action column at 620px; the port's transfer-list is a plain
2-column grid with no middle band. Structural, not a breakpoint — worth its own look.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-26 as NAMED BREAKPOINTS (web/app/globals.css @theme), not CSS classes.

Why not classes, given the .ns-grid2 precedent: a class carries the column TEMPLATE as well as the breakpoint, which would flatten sites that legitimately differ from the prototype's even split — working-time-fields' minmax(0,max-content)/minmax(0,1fr) Rest|Working row and optimize's 1fr/1.1fr. Named breakpoints single-source the VALUE, which is what actually drifted, and leave each site's template alone. Variants are named for the prototype class they come from (grid2:, grid3:, wizgrid:, wizgrid3:, formgrid:, panes2:) so a grid's breakpoint is traceable to the rule it implements.

Sites changed:
  save-load-workspace.tsx:86      lg -> grid2      (1024 -> 900)
  optimize-and-export-screen:360  lg -> grid2      (1024 -> 900)  [1fr/1.1fr ratio left as-is]
  home-guided.tsx:162             md/xl -> wizgrid/wizgrid3 (768/1280 -> 760/1200)
  requirement-form.tsx:265        md -> formgrid   (768 -> 720)
  contracted-form.tsx:562         sm -> formgrid   (640 -> 720)
  transfer-list.tsx:139           sm -> panes2     (640 -> 600)
  shift-type-grid.tsx:254         min-[1100px] -> grid3   (same value, now named)
  home-advanced.tsx:31            min-[1100px] -> grid3   (same value, now named)
  dates-screen.tsx:129            .ns-grid2 class -> grid2: utility; the class deleted from
                                  components/dates/calendar.css so one mechanism serves all sites

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN AUDIT. Row 5 was partly WRONG. It listed shift-type-grid's two inner form rows and working-time-fields' Rest|Working row as .ns-formgrid sites approximated at sm (640). They are not .ns-formgrid at all: the shift card's editing grid is the card's OWN inline rule, a flat 'grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr' with NO media query (ScreenShifts.dc.html:46). So sm there is our own concession to phones, not a stand-in for a prototype breakpoint, and changing it to formgrid: would have been a regression against the design AND would have disturbed the max-content split another agent had just measured. Left alone, with a comment at shift-type-grid.tsx:722 saying so. Only contracted-form from that row was a real .ns-formgrid site.

Also removed --breakpoint-xfer (620px) before it shipped: nothing uses it, because the port has no .ns-xfer three-column transfer list. Noted in globals.css to add it when that is implemented.

VERIFIED. Boundary probe in a live browser, 1px either side of every value: dates/save-load/optimize 899->1 col, 901->2; wizgrid 759->1, 761->2; wizgrid3 1199->2, 1201->3; grid3 1099->2, 1101->3. All seven media queries present in the generated CSS (600/720/760/900/1100/1200 + the 640 sm step). tsc clean, oxfmt clean, 2473 unit tests, 278 e2e all passing.

STILL OPEN, deliberately not changed here because they are visual and outside this bead: gap values differ from the prototype at several of these sites (save-load gap-6 vs .ns-grid2's space-4; contracted-form gap-4 and requirement-form gap-x-6/gap-y-5 vs .ns-formgrid's 20/24), and optimize's 1fr/1.1fr split against the prototype's even 1fr 1fr.
GAP + RATIO DEVIATIONS FIXED 2026-07-26, closing the follow-ups this bead recorded.

The prototype has its own density multiplier — --sp, Compact .8 / Comfortable 1 / Spacious 1.16, applied to --space-* (Nurse Scheduling.dc.html:25-26) — so whether a gap is a TOKEN or a LITERAL is load-bearing, not cosmetic. Ported accordingly:

  .ns-grid2   gap: var(--space-4)  -> TOKEN, scales   -> gap-4
  .ns-wizgrid gap: var(--space-3)  -> TOKEN, scales   -> gap-3 (already correct)
  .ns-formgrid gap: 20px 24px      -> LITERAL         -> gap-y-[20px] gap-x-[24px]
  .ns-panes2  gap: 12px            -> LITERAL         -> gap-[12px]

Changes:
  save-load-workspace.tsx   gap-6 -> gap-4                  (24 -> 16px, the class's token)
  optimize-and-export       gap-6 -> gap-4, + items-start,
                            grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_minmax(0,1.1fr)] -> grid-cols-2
                            (the right pane had 5% more than .ns-grid2 allows)
  contracted-form.tsx       gap-4 -> gap-x-[24px] gap-y-[20px]
  requirement-form.tsx      gap-x-6 gap-y-5 -> gap-x-[24px] gap-y-[20px]
  transfer-list.tsx         gap-3 -> gap-[12px]

CORRECTION to this bead's earlier note, which said requirement-form's gap deviated. At comfortable density gap-x-6/gap-y-5 IS 24/20 — it was already right. What was wrong there was subtler: those are scale utilities, so they rode the density multiplier where .ns-formgrid's literal does not. Same for transfer-list's gap-3. Both now literal, so they hold at 20/24 and 12 across all three densities as the prototype does.

VERIFIED in a live browser at comfortable and spacious:
  grid2 gap   16px -> 18.56px  (scales, = 16 x 1.16)
  panes2 gap  12px -> 12px     (literal, holds)
  optimize    cols 552/552 comfortable, 547.531/547.547 spacious — even within sub-pixel rounding
tsc clean, oxfmt clean, 2482 unit tests, 278 e2e all passing.

STILL OPEN, out of scope here and worth its own bead: the port folds the prototype's TWO multipliers into one. The prototype has --sp for spacing (Compact .8, Spacious 1.16) and --dens for type (Compact .9, Spacious 1.07); globals.css has a single --density (Compact .9, Spacious 1.16). So compact spacing is 12.5% roomier than the design and spacious type ~8% larger.

title: Screen width diverges from prototype: five per-screen max-w-* values vs one 1240px shell
description:
The prototype sets the content width ONCE, in the shell: `Nurse Scheduling.dc.html:137`
wraps every screen in `<div style="max-width:1240px;margin:0 auto;">` inside
`padding: var(--space-6) var(--space-5) 72px`. Every screen therefore renders at the
same 1240px.

The port has no width wrapper in `AppShell` (web/components/shell/app-shell.tsx:43 —
the scroll container renders `children` directly), so each screen sets its own
container and five different widths are in use:

| width | screens |
|---|---|
| `max-w-[1240px]` (matches prototype) | components/home/home-screen.tsx:40 |
| `max-w-6xl` (1152px) | components/shift-types/shift-type-grid.tsx:226, components/optimize/optimize-and-export-screen.tsx:337, app/optimize-screen-fixture/fixture-client.tsx:155 |
| `max-w-5xl` (1024px) | components/dates/dates-screen.tsx:107, components/people/people-table.tsx:182, components/guided-rules/rules-screen.tsx:134, components/card-editor/card-editor-shell.tsx:29, app/(app)/save-and-load/page.tsx:18 |
| `max-w-4xl` (896px) | components/requests/requests-editor.tsx:346 (empty state) |
| `max-w-[1400px]` | components/requests/requests-editor.tsx:401 (matrix) |

Home already uses 1240px, so the intent is on record — the rest drifted.

This is not only cosmetic. Measured 2026-07-26 while fixing the Shifts working-time
readout: the shift cards are a 3-up grid, so at a 1280px viewport each half-row field
inside a card is 126px against 166px in the prototype's shell. That is what made the
`WORKING · AUTO` derivation caption clip. Anything laid out inside a multi-column card
grid inherits the same squeeze.
design: Hoist the container into the shell so there is one source of truth: either wrap AppShell's scroll area (web/components/shell/app-shell.tsx:43) in the prototype's 1240px + px-5 py-8 box, or add a shared <Screen> wrapper the routes use, then strip the per-screen mx-auto/max-w-*/px-5/py-8. Two screens need an explicit call rather than a blind rewrite: the Requests matrix at max-w-[1400px] is WIDER than the prototype's shell (a wide-table screen — keep it as a documented exception or let the table scroll inside 1240px), and the max-w-5xl reading screens will get noticeably wider, which is the prototype's behaviour but is a visible change worth eyeballing per screen.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Screen width is set in exactly one place; no screen component carries its own max-w-*. 2. Every screen renders at the prototype's 1240px, or is listed as an explicit documented exception with a reason. 3. Visual pass on Shifts, Dates, Staff, Rules, Optimize, Save/Load, Requests at 1280 and 1600 viewports. 4. Existing unit + e2e suites pass (several specs assert layout-adjacent behaviour, none should need width edits).
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-26. AppShell (web/components/shell/app-shell.tsx) now wraps HydrationGate's children in the prototype's single container: mx-auto w-full max-w-[1240px] px-5 pb-18 pt-6 (Nurse Scheduling.dc.html:137 — max-width:1240px inside space-6/space-5/72px). Per-screen containers stripped from 9 call sites: home-screen, dates-screen, people-table, rules-screen, card-editor-shell (backs requirements/successions/counts/coverings/affinities), shift-type-grid, optimize-and-export-screen, save-and-load/page, requests-editor (both the empty state and the matrix). Screens now render a bare flex column. Exceptions and non-goals: hydration-gate keeps its own max-w-3xl/max-w-md centring because those states sit OUTSIDE the container by design; /design-system and the two fixtures under app/ (not app/(app)) render bare without AppShell and keep their own containers. Requests matrix: NO exception needed — it already has its own overflow-auto max-h-[68vh] scroller (requests-matrix.tsx:250), so 1240px just makes it scroll horizontally as the prototype's does, and max-w-[1400px] is retired.
REVIEW FIXES 2026-07-26 (cold review, artifacts/container-hoist-review). Two P2 fidelity defects found and fixed:

1. Cap and padding were on the same border-box div (max-w-[1240px] px-5), so content was 1200px, not 1240px — the change silently spent 40px of the cap on its own padding. The prototype nests them: padding on the outer box, cap on an unpadded inner one. Now two elements. Verified: content is 1240px at the cap.

2. pb-18 rode the density multiplier (globals.css drives Tailwind's --spacing off --space-1), giving 83.5px at spacious and 64.8px at compact where the prototype uses a LITERAL 72px. Now pb-[72px]. Top and sides are density-scaled in the prototype too, so pt-6 / px-5 stay as scale utilities. Verified across compact/comfortable/spacious: padding 21.6/18/72, 24/20/72, 27.84/23.2/72 — bottom fixed, top and sides scaling.

Review also confirmed: every product route under app/(app) inherits AppShell; card-editor routes and the durable optimize fixture are not double-wrapped; the Requests matrix has its own overflow-auto + minWidth:max-content scroll surface so retiring max-w-[1400px] is safe; the min-[1100px] variants correctly mirror .ns-grid3 and no other product lg:grid-cols-3 stands in for that ladder.

title: Tailwind v4 duration-token namespace mismatch (--duration-* vs --transition-duration-*)
description:
T03 ported --duration-fast/--duration-base into globals.css as plain CSS vars, but Tailwind v4's duration-* utilities are keyed off the --transition-duration-* namespace. As a result every duration-fast/duration-base class app-wide (button.tsx, switch.tsx, mobile-nav, possibly more) was silently emitting no utility and falling back to the default 150ms — the design's base(220ms)/fast(150ms) motion tokens were never actually applied as utilities.

The sidebar-fix agent worked around it locally (mobile-nav uses arbitrary [transition-duration:var(--dur-base)]), but the systemic fix is a one-line rename in globals.css: --duration-fast → --transition-duration-fast, --duration-base → --transition-duration-base (verify the exact Tailwind v4 namespace against the installed version via context7 first).

Verify against: docs/design_prototype (motion tokens), web/app/globals.css:348-350, and grep all duration-fast/duration-base usages. After the rename, audit that no transition silently changed timing in a regressions-introducing way (some may have been accidentally-correct at 150ms and should explicitly become duration-fast).

title: Ask how to set cors allowed domain ?
description: can we set it via env ? since env already sets the api domain
notes:
RESOLVED via the BFF architecture (DL11 D1 / tech-plan §3, ticket T06).

Q: can we set the CORS allowed domain via env, since env already sets the api domain?

A: You don't need to. Two parts:
1. NORMAL OPERATION — no CORS config needed. With the Next same-origin BFF, the browser only ever calls /api/* on the Next origin; the Next server calls the backend server-side inside the Docker network. The browser therefore NEVER triggers the backend's CORS allow-list, so the backend CORS domain is irrelevant to the deployed app. cloudflared fronts 'web'; 'web'->'backend' is server-side.
2. TODAY IT IS NOT ENV-DRIVEN — the backend CORS is a hardcoded regex in serve.py (allow_origin_regex = localhost | *.nursescheduling.org, C2 §Conformance). It is not read from env. The API domain the frontend uses is env (BACKEND_API_URL, server-side) — a different thing from the backend's CORS allow-list.
3. IF direct browser->backend access is ever wanted (bypassing the BFF) from a custom domain, making the CORS origin env-configurable would be a small backend config adaptation (same spirit as DL11 D2's version-fn change) — out of scope now; not required for the BFF deploy.
close_reason: Answered: BFF makes backend CORS config unnecessary for normal operation (same-origin); backend CORS is a hardcoded regex, not env — env only sets the server-side BACKEND_API_URL. See notes + DL11 D1 / T06.

title: Backfill CP-SAT oracle cases for the remaining 27 catalogue checks
description:
Only G7 has a committed oracle test (core/tests/test_catalogue_oracle_g7.py). The other 27 checks were verified during catalogue construction by agent runs whose harness was never committed, so the catalogue's soundness claim currently rests on history rather than on a running gate.

SCOPE (realistic, which is why this is NOT folded into s30): the committed harness ships ONE scenario builder (shift counts). Covering the full set needs roughly five more builders - staffing requirements, successions, affinities, coverings, and request/history pins - plus 27 predicates and several hundred candidate shapes. The G7 sweep runs in 0.49s, so runtime is not the constraint; authoring the shapes is.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT BUY - do not repeat the confusion this bead was split out of. The Python oracle asserts a PYTHON PREDICATE against CP-SAT. It never executes the TypeScript detector, so it validates the CATALOGUE, not the CODE. An implementation that mis-encodes check 12 in TS would still pass every oracle test. The TS side needs its own unit tests; the two are connected only by a SHARED FIXTURE CORPUS - express each check's candidate shapes once, in a form both suites consume, so the scenario CP-SAT proved infeasible is literally the scenario the detector is asserted to fire on.

METHOD (unchanged from G7): assert ONLY the sound direction - predicted infeasible implies the solver returns INFEASIBLE. Never assert the converse; catalogue checks are bounded relaxations, so a solver-proven-infeasible scenario may sit outside every check. Also pin each check's build-time premises the way G7 pins coefficient >= 1 and duplicate-coefficient rejection.
acceptance_criteria: Every catalogue check has oracle coverage asserting the sound direction, plus negative cases from the Rejected and NEEDS-SOLVER lists asserting silence. A shared fixture corpus exists that both the Python oracle and the TypeScript detector tests consume.

title: Consolidate five byte-identical expandDateRange copies onto lib/dates
description:
Five component model files each define a byte-identical expandDateRange(rangeStart, rangeEnd): string[] (md5 e44cc328eb5a1d39e64063efc6872171 across all five):
  web/components/affinities/affinities-model.ts:170
  web/components/successions/successions-model.ts:155
  web/components/requirements/requirements-model.ts:253
  web/components/coverings/coverings-model.ts:210
  web/components/counts/counts-model.ts:226
Each expands an inclusive ISO range into concrete ISO dates, returning [] for a missing/invalid/reversed range.

THE TARGET IS NOT generateDateIds. That returns SPAN-COMPRESSED date IDS (DD / MM-DD / YYYY-MM-DD via formatId(iso, spanClass(range))), whereas expandDateRange returns BARE ISO strings. Substituting one for the other would silently change the values these date-scope UIs work with - a bug, not a cleanup. An earlier note on s30 claimed generateDateIds was the canonical home; that was wrong.

THE CORRECT SOURCE is generateDateItems(range) in web/lib/dates/date-id.ts:117, which returns DateItem[] carrying BOTH { id (span-formatted), iso, description }. The canonical ISO expansion is therefore generateDateItems(range).map(i => i.iso). Either use that directly or add a small named helper (e.g. expandIsoRange) beside it in lib/dates so the intent is explicit at call sites.

SIGNATURE DIFFERENCE: the copies take (rangeStart: string, rangeEnd: string); the canonical takes a DateRange. Call sites need adapting.

VERIFY EQUIVALENCE BEFORE SWAPPING - do not assume. The copies guard on empty string, Date.parse NaN, and start > end. generateDateItems guards on !hasCompleteRange(range). Confirm they agree on: empty/missing endpoints, malformed ISO, a reversed range, and single-day ranges. If they differ anywhere, fix the guard rather than silently changing behaviour at five call sites.

WHY IT MATTERS: five copies of a date expansion is a drift hazard in exactly the area date semantics are already delicate (span-compressed ids, the range-change cascade that re-keys ids when the span class changes, and bead rf3 which proposes retiring span compression entirely). If rf3 lands, five copies are five places to miss.
design: Test-covered refactor, no behaviour change intended. Each of the five model files has adjacent tests; run them plus the card-editor e2e for the affected screens (affinities, successions, requirements, coverings, counts). Deliberately NOT folded into s30 (Tier-1 checks): s30 needs date IDS via generateDateIds/expandDateRefs, not this ISO expander, and pulling five shipped components into that initiative would widen its blast radius for no benefit.
acceptance_criteria: One ISO-range expansion implementation in lib/dates, used by all five call sites; the five local copies deleted; existing tests for all five screens pass unchanged; no change to the values any date-scope UI produces.

title: Optimize panel: retire 'Resubmit' for one honest 'Run again' verb; verdict box still open
description:
Two related honesty problems on the Optimize infeasible panel, found by cold critique 2026-07-27 (reviews/two-tier-revision-critique).

1. 'TRY AGAIN' AFTER A PROOF. The panel states the solver PROVED no roster satisfies every hard rule, then offers 'Try again' beside it. Re-running an unchanged scenario cannot succeed, so the control implies someone is still looking - which directly undermines flow state D2's requirement that the panel must not imply further investigation. Worse, resubmit re-derives from the LIVE store (web/components/optimize/optimize-and-export-screen.tsx:230), so 'Try again' silently runs a DIFFERENT scenario than the one just proven infeasible, with no indication that it changed. Consider: disable or relabel until the scenario changes, or make the re-derivation explicit.

2. A CONSTANT PRESENTED AS SOLVER DATA. Both wireframes render 'verdict: infeasibility_proven' in a monospace data box, but that string is a HARDCODED literal at core/nurse_scheduling/server/jobs/runner.py:97 - we set it unconditionally on the INFEASIBLE branch. It carries zero information beyond the heading already shown. Presenting our own constant in a data-looking box is the same provenance failure the rule-conflict-validation flow polices for its own findings. Note this partially qualifies decisions/prototype-backend-capability, which described it as a solver-emitted verdict that 'is present, not optional' - true, but only because we always write it.
acceptance_criteria: The infeasible panel does not imply continued investigation, does not silently resubmit a different scenario than the one proven infeasible, and does not present an app-authored constant as solver-returned data.
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-07-27. VERDICT ON ITEM 1: SPEC GAP, NOT A BUG - and the critique's framing was overstated.

WHY IT IS NOT A BUG. Re-deriving from the live store is deliberate, documented, and correct for the designed flow. run-status-panel.tsx:18 states it outright: 'The infeasible Try again and the idle CTA reuse the run-start path.' The panel copy at :220 says 'Loosen a hard rule and try again' - i.e. the intended journey is Adjust rules -> change something -> Try again. Picking up those changes is the POINT. The critique's characterisation ('silently runs a DIFFERENT scenario with no indication that it changed') describes the feature working as designed, not a defect. Rejecting that part.

THE REAL AND NARROWER GAP. Try again is offered UNCONDITIONALLY, including when nothing has changed. In that case the user re-runs a scenario CP-SAT already PROVED infeasible: same answer guaranteed, wall-clock wasted, and the control implies 'maybe this time' - exactly what flow state D2 forbids the panel from implying. optimize-run-outcome lists Try again as an unconditional action and is silent on change detection. That silence is the gap.

SECOND ISSUE THE CRITIQUE DID NOT NAME - shared handler, divergent promises. run-status-panel.tsx:166-167 is one button relabelled: {workerLost ? 'Resubmit' : 'Try again'}, onClick={onResubmit}; the infeasible panel's separate button at :236 calls the same onResubmit. Both route to optimize-and-export-screen.tsx:243 -> buildSubmitInput() -> toCanonicalScenarioDocument(useScenarioStore.getState()) at :230. For infeasible that is right. For worker_lost it is a semantic mismatch: 'Resubmit' promises re-sending WHAT WAS SENT (the run died through no fault of the scenario), but it sends current state. If the user edited while the run was in flight and the worker then died, Resubmit silently submits a different scenario under a label promising otherwise. Rare path, but the word carries the promise. Spec is silent on what Resubmit re-sends.

NO CONFLICT WITH THE TIER-1 CARRY-FORWARD DESIGN: a new run carries its own new finding set, so s30 is unaffected either way.

POSSIBLE DIRECTION (not decided): the scenario store already maintains backupFingerprint, so 'changed since this run' is cheaply detectable - could gate/relabel Try again and disambiguate Resubmit. Needs a product call, not just an edit.
SETTLED 2026-07-27 (item 1 only; item 2 remains open).

DECISION - ONE VERB, ONE PROMISE. Every re-run control on the Optimize screen becomes 'Run again' and submits the CURRENT setup. Applies to infeasible, cancelled, and the resubmittable failed states.

'RESUBMIT' IS RETIRED. The word promised re-sending the exact submitted document; the code never did that - all paths go through toCanonicalScenarioDocument(useScenarioStore.getState()) at optimize-and-export-screen.tsx:230. Keeping the promise would require retaining the submitted document, which T16q forbids ('do not record a scenario backup', 'do not add a second safety journal'). Rather than build retention for a word, the word goes.

NO CHANGE DETECTION (deliberate). computeScenarioFingerprint (web/lib/scenario/hash.ts) exists and would have made 'has anything changed since this run' cheap, but the user chose simplicity. The label is CONSTANT and never varies on whether the scenario changed. The verb change carries most of the honesty benefit on its own: 'Try again' implies a different outcome is possible; 'Run again' is outcome-neutral.

ACCEPTED RESIDUAL: on an infeasible run with nothing changed, Run again burns a run and returns the same proof. Judged cheaper than a fingerprint comparison plus the extra copy states and test surface.

worker_lost STAYS UNGATED - the run died for infrastructure reasons, so retrying identical input is the CORRECT action and must stay frictionless. Only the label changed. The server-authoritative view.resubmittable flag remains the sole gate (run-status-panel.tsx:160-167).

KNOCK-ON: the s30 submission-session-record change stays a SINGLE findings field - no fingerprint needed, since change detection was declined.

IMPLEMENTATION SURFACE: run-status-panel.tsx:167 (the workerLost ternary - delete it, always 'Run again'), :237 (infeasible button label), and the two test expectations in run-status-panel.test.tsx:187/211. Artifacts updated: optimize-run-outcome (new 'What the re-run controls promise' section, result table, lifecycle diagram, wireframe) and rule-conflict-validation state D wireframe.

STILL OPEN - ITEM 2: 'verdict: infeasibility_proven' is rendered in a monospace data box (run-status-panel.tsx:224-226) but is a hardcoded literal at core/nurse_scheduling/server/jobs/runner.py:97, carrying no information beyond the heading. Not settled here; needs its own call.
close_reason:
BOTH ITEMS SETTLED 2026-07-27. Spec-only; implementation surface listed below.

ITEM 1 - ONE VERB, ONE PROMISE. Every re-run control becomes 'Run again' and submits the CURRENT setup. 'Resubmit' retired: it promised re-sending the exact submitted document, which the code never did (all paths go through toCanonicalScenarioDocument(useScenarioStore.getState()) at optimize-and-export-screen.tsx:230), and honouring it would need document retention that T16q forbids. worker_lost stays UNGATED - retrying identical input is correct there; only the label changed. NO change detection (deliberate): the label is constant. Accepted residual: an unchanged infeasible re-run burns a run and returns the same proof.

ITEM 2 - THE VERDICT BOX IS DROPPED, AND THE REAL SIGNAL IS SURFACED. Investigation found termination_reason was rendered exactly where it means nothing and hidden exactly where it means something:
- INFEASIBLE: 'infeasibility_proven' is a hardcoded literal on a single branch (runner.py:97), 1:1 with the heading. Zero information, rendered in a monospace box implying machine-returned data. DROPPED.
- OPTIMAL: 'optimality_proven', 1:1 with solverStatus. Not shown, unchanged.
- FEASIBLE: 'user_requested' vs 'solver_timeout' - the ONLY branch where it varies, and it was never displayed. The success grid shows solverStatus/score/elapsed only (run-status-panel.tsx:200-211). NOW SURFACED as a plain-language line under the heading: solver_timeout -> 'the timeout expired before the solver could confirm this is the best possible roster - a longer timeout may score better'; user_requested -> 'you asked for results before the solver finished - a longer run may score better'; absent/unrecognised -> render nothing, never invent a reason.
Fidelity: a line under the heading, NOT a fourth grid cell - the three-cell grid is prototype-fidelity-reviewed and unchanged.

PRIOR DECISION AMENDED: decisions/prototype-backend-capability settled 'render whatever reason is non-null as a verdict'. Amended in place. Its INTENT (do not fabricate a conflict list; never present our output as the solver's diagnosis) is unchanged - dropping the label serves that intent rather than reversing it. What the original did not establish is that the constant is informative.

IMPLEMENTATION SURFACE:
- run-status-panel.tsx:167 - delete the workerLost ternary, always 'Run again'
- run-status-panel.tsx:237 - infeasible button label -> 'Run again'
- run-status-panel.tsx:222-227 - delete the terminationReason verdict block
- run-status-panel.tsx success block (~:199) - add the feasible-only stop-reason line

- the .reason CSS class in the optimize-run-outcome wireframe is now unused

title: Layout-ladder classes: sibling spacing still pivots on type breakpoints (sm/md) not their own
description:
RETRACTED AS ORIGINALLY FRAMED, then rescoped. The premise was wrong.

ORIGINAL CLAIM: bmw.8's baked 0.9 left ~78 arbitrary exact-px spacing sites rendering ~11% looser than their scaled-utility neighbours, so they were the anomaly and needed sweeping onto the 0.9 grid.

WHY THAT WAS WRONG: the 0.9 applies to the SCALE, not to every number. The codebase already had a deliberate, documented convention:
  - prototype var(--space-N)  -> scale utility (gap-6, pt-6)   -> renders x 0.9
  - prototype literal px      -> arbitrary value (pb-[72px])   -> renders exactly as designed
An arbitrary-px spacing value is therefore the CORRECT port of a prototype literal, not drift. Three instances, all authored with the 0.9 baseline explicitly in view:
  - app-shell.tsx:60  'The 72px bottom is LITERAL, as in the prototype ... so pb-18 would resolve to 64.8px.'
  - contracted-form.tsx:565  'Gap is the class's literal 20/24, not the 16px this used to carry.'
  - select.tsx:20  the converse — a value deliberately wired to --spacing 'exactly as pr-7 would'.
Sweeping would have reverted all three and tightened ~78 sites the design fixes. bmw.7 is NOT superseded.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BROKEN (fixed): CardEditorForm's body padding in card-editor-shell.tsx.
  was:  p-[18px] sm:px-7 sm:py-6
  now:  p-[18px] formgrid:px-[28px] formgrid:py-[26px]
Two independent defects, both real regardless of the scale rule:
  1. Wrong values — px-7/py-6 resolved to 25.2/21.6px where .ns-formbody says 26/28px (Nurse Scheduling.dc.html:96-97).
  2. Wrong breakpoint — sm: is 640px; the class pivots at 720px. That is the formgrid breakpoint bmw.7 added and used for the grid INSIDE this very body, without moving the body's own padding onto it.
Verified: tsc, oxlint, oxfmt clean; 2430 unit tests pass.

REMAINING (why this stays open at P3): the sm:-vs-layout-ladder mistake in item 2 is the generalisable one. bmw.7 moved nine GRID call sites onto the ladder but not the paddings and other spacing that belong to the same .ns-* classes. Audit the rest of the layout ladder's classes for sibling properties still pivoting on a type-scale breakpoint (sm/md/lg) instead of their own. Do NOT re-open the literal-vs-utility question — see the decision artifact.

Decision artifact: .traycer/epics/8b2235d5-8943-4f6d-a61e-3b671836217a/artifacts/app-prototype-fidelity-audit/decisions/baked-0-9-spacing-and-type-scale/index.md
notes:
GOVERNING QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED (user, 2026-07-26) — do not re-litigate.

The baked 0.9 is INTENTIONAL on both the spacing grid and the type ramp. Recorded in:
.traycer/epics/8b2235d5-8943-4f6d-a61e-3b671836217a/artifacts/app-prototype-fidelity-audit/decisions/baked-0-9-spacing-and-type-scale/index.md

Consequences for this bead:
- The rule is 'prototype value x 0.9'. Scaled utilities are CORRECT; gap-3 = 10.8px is the intended rendering of a prototype 12px literal.
- The ~78 arbitrary exact-px spacing sites across 25 files are the anomaly — each renders ~11% looser than its neighbours on the grid. They are the sweep target, NOT the ~915 utility sites.
- bmw.7's exact-px gaps (.ns-formgrid 20/24px, .ns-panes2 12px) are SUPERSEDED. Its token-vs-literal reasoning was right for a world with a multiplier; bmw.8 removed the multiplier, so there is nothing left for the distinction to express.

Remaining choice is mechanical, not a product call: prefer a utility (gap-6) where the value lands on the 4px grid; use calc(Npx * 0.9) only for off-grid prototype values.

The card-editor-shell.tsx:269 instance in the description still stands, and its wrong-breakpoint half (sm: 640px vs .ns-formbody's 720px formgrid) is independent of the scale rule — fix that regardless.
close_reason:
Audit complete. The ladder is in better shape than the bead assumed — one real fix, one deliberate exception confirmed, everything else already correct.

METHOD: read every .ns-* layout class and ALL its responsive properties from Nurse Scheduling.dc.html:76-97 (not just grid-template-columns), then checked each app call site plus every sm:/md:/lg:/xl: responsive spacing or layout utility in components/ and app/.

FIXED — components/shell/top-bar.tsx: px-4 sm:px-5 -> px-5.
The prototype header is 'padding:0 var(--space-5)' with NO media query (Nurse Scheduling.dc.html:122). The sm: step pivoted at 640px, a breakpoint the design does not have, and it tightened the phone case to 14.4px vs the designed 18px — backwards, since the rail is hidden below 920px so there is more room, not less. Commented in place.

CONFIRMED CORRECT (no change):
- All nine bmw.7 sites still wired: panes2 (transfer-list), formgrid (requirement-form, contracted-form), wizgrid + wizgrid3 (home-guided), grid2 (dates, save-load, optimize), grid3 (shift-types, home-advanced), nav (app-shell, top-bar).
- .ns-grid3's SECOND step at 640px is genuinely sm: — the prototype's own value, not a type-step stand-in. Already commented at shift-type-grid.tsx:250.
- .ns-formbody (720px) had exactly one consumer, CardEditorForm — fixed in the prior turn (formgrid:px-[28px] formgrid:py-[26px]). The class is ScreenCards-only, so the flat p-[18px] on other screens' panels is correct; they are not .ns-formbody.
- .ns-xfer (620px) correctly omitted — the port has no three-column transfer list (bmw.7 documented this).
- shift-type-grid's two inner form rows and the working-time Rest|Working row keep sm: as a phone concession — commented, bmw.7 documented.
- top-bar h-14 (50.4px vs the prototype's literal 56px) is DELIBERATE: documented in the file header ('the shell scales with the content it frames') and pinned by an e2e geometry check (nursing-sheduler-yea). Left alone.

NOTED, NOT A LADDER DEFECT:
- components/home/home-stat-strip.tsx uses 'grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-5' where the prototype stat strip is 'display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:0' with no media query at all (ScreenHome.dc.html:23). The sm: pivot is invented, but so is the whole grid-vs-flex-wrap approach — a port technique choice, not a breakpoint standing in for a prototype value. Not changed; raise separately if the wrap behaviour is wanted.
- app/design-system/page.tsx uses sm:/lg: grids freely; it is the token showcase, not product UI.

Verified: tsc, oxlint, oxfmt clean; 2430 unit tests; 275 Playwright e2e against a production build.

title: Reconcile shadow tokens: --shadow-toast is dead, Switch thumb is off-token
description:
Surfaced by the cold review of the /design-system guide rewrite (artifact design-system-page-audit-review).

Two inconsistencies in the shadow layer. Both are recorded truthfully on the guide page now, so nothing is hidden - but they are worth reconciling.

1. --shadow-toast is declared in globals.css (:root and @theme inline) and reached for by NOTHING. The toast it is named for, .ns-toast, uses var(--shadow-side) instead. Either wire .ns-toast to --shadow-toast (its named purpose, a softer 0 8px 26px) or delete the token. Note the two shadows differ visually: --shadow-side is a directional -16px 0 40px drawer shadow, so switching .ns-toast to --shadow-toast IS a visual change to the toast, not a no-op rename.

2. components/ui/switch.tsx:26 - the Switch thumb uses Tailwind's default shadow-sm, the only shadow in components/ui that is not a design token. The existing raw-color source guard over components/ui/** does not cover shadows, so nothing flagged it.
