Related dead token, same shape of problem: --t-h2 / text-h2 has zero usages and is an exact alias of text-display. Worth deciding at the same time.

title: e2e drag simulations wait a fixed 50ms for drag state instead of a condition
description:
Found by the arbitrary-wait sweep after the 02h flake fix. These are the waitForTimeout calls that nursing-sheduler-5e2 does NOT cover: 5e2 is scoped to persistence waits (its acceptance criterion is the authoritative saved-state seam) and only one call in the suite is that.

Five sites simulate HTML5 drag-and-drop in the same shape: dispatch `dragstart` in one page.evaluate, `await page.waitForTimeout(50)`, then dispatch dragover/drop in a second evaluate. The 50ms is a guess at how long React needs to register the drag state before the drop is meaningful.

  web/e2e/affinities.spec.ts    (affinity-card-0 -> affinity-card-2)
  web/e2e/counts.spec.ts        (count-card-0 -> count-card-2)
  web/e2e/requirements.spec.ts  (requirement-card-0 -> requirement-card-2)
  web/e2e/successions.spec.ts   (succession-card-0 -> succession-card-2)
  web/e2e/successions.spec.ts   (pattern-chip-0 -> pattern-chip-2)

Not currently failing — the full suite passed 834/834 at --repeat-each=3 and the geometry specs 864/864 at --repeat-each=12 during the sweep. This is latent: 50ms is unvalidated, so it is slow on a fast machine and a coin flip on a loaded one, exactly the shape of the 02h flake before it started failing.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE, the other six waits, because the elapsed time IS the assertion and converting them would delete what is being tested:
- app-shell.spec.ts 300ms — URL still /shift-types (guards a delayed history.back())
- optimize-progress-chart.spec.ts 300ms x2 — tap-retained tooltip still visible after a pause
- optimize-assembled-stream.spec.ts — keepalive window, then assert a real ": keepalive" chunk arrived; and 2s post-navigation abort teardown
- optimize-durable-stream.spec.ts 1s — allow one controller poll/reconnect turn, then assert nothing unlocked incorrectly
You cannot poll for a non-event. If these are ever touched it should be to name the durations as shared constants, not to make them conditions.
design:
Replace the sleep with a wait on the drag state the app actually sets. The drop evaluate already reaches into the DOM by data-testid, so the condition wants to be whatever dragstart flips — a dragging attribute/class on the source card, or the store field the card editors set. Confirm which by reading the drag handlers in the card-editor components rather than assuming; if nothing observable is set, the honest fix is to expose one for the test rather than keep a magic 50ms.

Keep the two-evaluate structure: it is deliberate, since the DataTransfer has to survive between dragstart and drop via window.__dt.
acceptance_criteria: No waitForTimeout remains in the five drag simulations; each waits on an observable drag state. The four affected specs pass at --repeat-each=12, and still fail if the drop is dispatched without a preceding dragstart.
notes:
DONE (uncommitted in the working tree).

The drag state existed but was not observable: CardListItem rendered isDragging only as an opacity-50 class, and PatternChip did the same. Waiting on a Tailwind class would have coupled the specs to styling, so per the design note the hook is now explicit — data-dragging="true", following the data-disabled convention already on the same elements. Two source lines:

  components/card-editor/card-editor-shell.tsx  CardListItem <li>   (covers affinities, counts, requirements, successions cards)
  components/successions/pattern-builder.tsx    PatternChip <span>  (covers the pattern chips)

All five specs now wait on it instead of sleeping:
  await expect(page.getByTestId("<card>-0")).toHaveAttribute("data-dragging", "true");
toHaveAttribute auto-retries, so this is condition-based rather than a poll loop written by hand. Zero waitForTimeout calls remain in the four drag specs.

VERIFIED in a worktree isolated from other agents in-flight edits, production build:
- affinities + counts + requirements + successions at --repeat-each=12 -> 972 passed, 0 failed.
- Load-bearing, not vacuous: deleting the dragstart dispatch makes the test FAIL at the wait with "expect(locator).toHaveAttribute(expected) failed", not pass through it.

Side benefit worth keeping: the failure is now legible. Previously a broken dragstart slept 50ms and then failed at the final order assertion, which reads as a reorder bug; it now fails at the wait and names the missing drag state.

tsc, oxlint and oxfmt clean. The source change is additive — a data attribute, no behaviour, no styling.
close_reason: Closed

title: Progress chart paints at 800px before ResizeObserver measures, overflowing narrow viewports
description:
Found while root-causing the 02h e2e flake. The flake is fixed; THIS is the real behaviour underneath it, and it is not a test artifact.

components/optimize/progress-chart/progress-chart.tsx holds DEFAULT_CONTAINER_WIDTH = 800 in useState and only replaces it when a ResizeObserver effect reports the real container width. ProgressPanel renders <svg width={containerWidth}>, so the chart paints 800px wide on first render regardless of viewport.

On a 375px device that means the page genuinely overflows horizontally by 475px until the observer fires — a visible sideways jolt or scrollbar flash on first paint, on the narrowest devices we support. Measured in a real browser, not inferred: scrollWidth 850 vs clientWidth 375, with the score-panel SVG at w=800 right=850.

Not urgent: the window is one frame or two, and it self-corrects. But it is a real first-paint defect on mobile and the narrow-card bands this project has been tightening elsewhere.
design:
The obvious fix — lower the fallback — just moves the problem, since any fixed fallback is wrong at some viewport. Better directions:

- Render the SVG responsively (width="100%" with the viewBox already present) so it scales to its container regardless of the measured number, and keep containerWidth only for the geometry maths.
- Or hold first paint until measured: render the frame/skeleton at container width and the plot only once containerWidth has been set from a real measurement.

CONSTRAINT that makes this non-trivial, and the reason it was not folded into the 02h fix: DEFAULT_CONTAINER_WIDTH is load-bearing for the jsdom unit suite. components/optimize/progress-chart/progress-chart.test.tsx stubs out ResizeObserver precisely so the chart falls back to 800 and its geometry assertions stay deterministic, and it also stubs getBoundingClientRect to an 800-wide rect for the hover tests. Changing the render strategy means reworking those fixtures, so it wants its own pass rather than riding along with a test-flake fix.
acceptance_criteria: At a 375px viewport, the optimize screen never exceeds the viewport width at any point during first paint (assert without polling — measure immediately after the chart is visible). The jsdom progress-chart suite still passes with deterministic geometry.
notes: Thin mirror. Source: /home/kenan/.traycer/epics/8b2235d5-8943-4f6d-a61e-3b671836217a/artifacts/progress-chart-first-paint-responsive/index.md

title: DR-5 follow-up: one native-select treatment (caret padding) across the app
description:
User-reported: every <select> in the app rendered its dropdown caret flush against the right border with no gap (screenshot: the Shift Types "TIME ON FLOOR" pair).

ROOT CAUSE: Chrome paints the native select arrow INSIDE the element's padding-right, so the px-2 (8px) these controls used was entirely consumed by the ~16px arrow, which then overlapped the border.

The design prototype already solved this for ONE select — ScreenRules.dc.html:38-40 uses appearance:none with padding:0 34px 0 12px plus an absolutely positioned CSS triangle in --ink3 at right:13px — but only the Rules constraint picker was ported that way. The shift-time selects (ScreenShifts.dc.html:60-67,77) were left on the platform arrow, so they inherited the crowding.

FIX: extract the prototype treatment into a single primitive rather than patching padding per call site.
design:
web/components/ui/select.tsx (new): wrapper span + appearance-none select with pr-7 reserved for the caret, and the prototype triangle (10x6, --ink3) at right-2.5. Prototype fixed px translated to Tailwind scale steps so the caret spacing tracks --density (data-density 0.9/1.0/1.16) like the rest of the spacing scale. fullWidth prop applies w-full to wrapper + select.

Call sites converted (4 selects, 2 files) — these are ALL the native <select> elements in web/; every other dropdown-looking control is a custom button/popover and is unaffected:
- web/components/entity-editor/working-time-fields.tsx — start / end / rest
- web/components/guided-rules/pin-form.tsx — constraint picker (was appearance-default despite the prototype specifying otherwise)

KNOWN FOOTGUN (flagged in the review): the primitive keeps pl-2 pr-7 in its base classes, so a caller passing px-* would have tailwind-merge drop the pr-7 and silently reinstate the bug. Currently guarded only by a doc comment. A regression test pinning the reserved padding was NOT added — see notes.
acceptance_criteria: Every native select reserves space for its caret: appearance:none, caret-to-border gap and value-to-caret gap both non-zero at all three density settings. Verified in-browser on /shift-types at default density — all three time selects report appearance:none, padding-right 28px, caret-to-border 10px, value-to-caret 8px.
notes:
VALIDATION: web/ pnpm typecheck clean; oxlint clean; pnpm test 160 files / 2473 passed, 63 skipped. Geometry measured in a real Chromium against the running dev server (Playwright, /shift-types add-shift form).

NO REGRESSION TEST ADDED. The behaviour worth pinning is that the primitive always reserves right padding for the caret and that no caller overrides it away with px-*. A design-system-style vitest assertion (the suite already has one forbidding lucide-react imports) is the natural home. Left out of the fix deliberately, called out for the reviewer to rule on.

A cold review is in flight — Codex gpt-5.6-terra, Traycer agent a9756756, asked to judge the pr-7/caret-offset relationship across densities, whether the px-* footgun needs API enforcement rather than a comment, label association for the span-wrapped select inside pin-form label, and whether the font-weight change below belongs.

SCOPE ADDITION (flagged to the user): the time selects previously carried no font-weight while the prototype specifies 600 for start/end and 700 for rest, so font-semibold/font-bold were added in the same edit. Trivially revertible — two classes.
RESOLVED in be41ad9 (branch dr4-dr5-fidelity).

Cold review (Codex gpt-5.6-terra) came back with no P1 and two findings, both fixed before the commit — artifacts/select-primitive-padding-review:
- P2 the reserved gutter was overridable. Review suggested merging pr-7 AFTER className. Tried it and it is NOT sufficient: tailwind-merge keeps both, yielding "px-3 pr-7", so the winner falls to stylesheet source order rather than anything the component controls (the first test written against that assumption failed and showed it). Settled on an INLINE STYLE, calc(var(--spacing) * 7) — the only mechanism a caller class cannot defeat, still density-scaled, and it also survives a caller passing their own style object.
- P3 the sibling caret stayed opaque on a disabled select where the native arrow used to fade. Fixed with peer / peer-disabled:opacity-60. Verified in-browser: caret opacity 1 -> 0.6, matching the control.

TEST ADDED after all: web/components/ui/select.test.tsx, 8 cases pinning the gutter invariant (incl. the px-* and inline-style override attempts), the decorative-caret contract, and the fullWidth seam.

Density sweep in Chromium — gutter 25.2 / 28 / 32.5px and value-to-caret 6.2 / 8 / 10.9px at compact / comfortable / spacious.

COMMIT SCOPE: working-time-fields.tsx carries concurrent in-flight work by another agent (decimal-hour readout, caption layout). Only the caret lines were staged, via a hand-built blob; the staged tree was typechecked and unit-tested in isolation (2472 passed) before committing so the commit is green on its own. The readout work remains uncommitted for its owner.

title: guided-rules e2e: AdjustPanel commits on blur/Enter — .fill() alone won't persist
description:
Convention/gotcha for guided-rules Adjust e2e tests.

AdjustPanel (web/components/guided-rules/rule-row.tsx) deliberately commits a quick-field edit ONLY on blur or Enter: onChange updates a local draft (live feedback) but never writes the store, so the whole adjust is a single zundo entry (not one per keystroke). Playwright's .fill() sets the value and fires input/change but does NOT blur or press Enter, so the mutateScenario write never fires and the card value is unchanged.

This bit rules.spec.ts:87 ('a requirement card derives a linked row; Toggle and Adjust write the same card') — a deterministic, pre-existing failure surfaced by the DR e2e run. Fixed by adding await adjustInput.press('Enter') after .fill('6').

CONVENTION for any future guided-rules Adjust e2e: when driving a rule-adjust-input-* field via .fill(), always follow with .press('Enter') (or .blur()) to trigger the commit, and poll the store for the committed value. Do NOT change AdjustPanel to commit on every keystroke — the commit-on-blur/Enter design is intentional (one undo entry per edit).

Refs: web/e2e/rules.spec.ts:116 (fixed example); AdjustPanel commit logic in rule-row.tsx (onBlur/onKeyDown Enter -> commitRaw). Currently only rules.spec.ts drives rule-adjust-input; this is preventive for future specs.

title: AI Infeasibility Diagnostician (Tier 2) — planned, brief later
description: PLACEHOLDER initiative (orientation only, brief later). Post-run AI: on infeasible, hypothesize -> re-run backend to test -> propose VERIFIED fixes. Tier 2 backstop to static Tier 1. OPTIONAL: off by default, single AI-features gate (toggle + BYO LLM key OpenRouter/Anthropic/OpenAI), CLIENT-SIDE DIRECT (key local in browser, calls straight to provider, nothing via backend). Open: agent loop, backend test-run budget/cost/safety, propose-vs-auto-apply, BYO-key storage/CORS/provider abstraction, reconcile l3m. Governed by decisions/path-to-feasibility-two-tier. Brief: .traycer/.../briefs/ai-infeasibility-diagnostician
notes:
RUN-SLOT SETTLED 2026-07-28 (D26/D27 in artifacts/ai-assistant/decisions).

GROUNDING: docker/.env.example states 'the reviewed one-worker deployment' (DIAGNOSTIC_EXPECTED_CONCURRENCY=1); worker.py claims jobs serially in a while-not-stop loop via claim_next_job. Pending capacity is 8, so the backend DOES queue and 'Queued' is already a modelled lifecycle state.

D26 - A Tier-2 verification check is REFUSED while the run slot is busy, whether by an optimize run or by another check. Sharing was never a product option: concurrent solving needs a second worker, i.e. a deployment change. Refusing avoids trading a real roster solve for a hypothetical one and prevents a check wedging the slot ordinary runs depend on. Contention is rare in practice because diagnosis follows a run that has already settled - an active optimize run only exists if the user deliberately started one. REQUIREMENT: the refusal must name the blocker ('a run is in progress - you can check this once it finishes') and re-enable itself automatically. Not a dead greyed-out button, and not something the user must reopen the panel to clear.

D27 - A check MUST NOT write to the optimize submission record, and is NOT resumable across a reload. The browser keeps a single in-flight submission record (web/lib/optimize/session-transaction.ts, key nurse.optimize.session) and that record is what a reload uses to decide there is a run to restore. A check writing to it would make a refresh restore the CHECK as the user's roster run, against a scenario copy that is not theirs. A check needs its own state; a refresh abandons it and returns the fix to Proposed. Losing a check on reload is cheap - re-run it - and far better than corrupting run recovery.

REJECTED: queue behind the active run (backend supports it, but a check could sit behind a multi-minute solve while the user waits on a yes/no, and it needs its own recovery record plus queue-position UI for a rare case); offer to cancel the active run (wrong priority, and cancel already exists on the run).

title: Backend: keyless elastic/slack re-solve for infeasible runs (replaces unsat-core plan)
description:
REWRITTEN 2026-07-27 (was: infeasibility conflict-explanation via CP-SAT sufficient-assumptions / minimal unsatisfiable core). The MECHANISM is superseded; the PURPOSE is retained.

WHY THE UNSAT CORE IS OUT (measured against pinned ortools==9.15.6755): the model must have NO objective at all - with a real objective the core returns ALL assumptions (32 of 32), with maximize(0) still all 10, and only with the objective removed entirely does it narrow (2 of 32). scheduler.py:277 sets an objective unconditionally, so a core needs a second, objective-free solve of a differently-built model. CP-SAT also auto-forces single-threading and weakens presolve under assumptions - a model proven infeasible in 3s across 8 workers may not re-prove in 300s. The core is 'sufficient' not minimal, returns EMPTY when the infeasibility is outside the gated set, and the structural constraints (one day-state per person-day, leave pinning) must not be gated or the core answers 'nurses can only work one shift a day' - yet they are co-conspirators in most real coverage failures. NOTE: these assumption-behaviour numbers come from a research probe against ortools directly, not from this repo (no CP-SAT assumptions exist in core/); re-measure before ever reversing this.

WHY THE NEED REMAINS: flow state D2 - Tier 1's checks found nothing and the solver still proved it impossible - is the DEFAULT experience for every user with AI off. Tier 1 (s30) cannot close it (the cause is outside the 27 by definition). Tier 2 (3d4) cannot close it for the default user (opt-in, needs a BYO key). This bead is the only path that answers D2 without an LLM.

REWRITTEN AS: elastic/slack re-solve - ONE extra multi-threaded solve (no assumption penalty, no forced sequential search) reporting HOW MUCH each rule must loosen. 'Coverage on 3 Aug is short by 3 nurses.' 'P7's contract exceeds capacity by 16 hours.' A repair, not a conflict set. Keyless, deterministic, always-on-capable - it belongs on the default path, NOT inside the optional AI tier (an earlier draft misfiled it under Tier 2).
design:
Additive backend capability on the C2 result contract, then rendered in the Optimize infeasible panel below the Tier-1 replay. Must respect the zero-drift vendored-backend posture (docs/T19-upstream-backend-source-manifest.md): net-new modules plus small documented edits, solver core untouched.

NOT a Tier-1 dependency. s30 ships without this and state D2 renders the honest scope sentence until it exists. Tier 2 (3d4) may USE it if present but does not own it.

Open: cost/wall-clock ceiling of the extra solve; which rule families get slack variables; how 'loosen by N' maps onto the shared conflict model so it renders through the same surface.

Governed by decisions/path-to-feasibility-two-tier (revised 2026-07-27) and reviews/two-tier-revision-critique.
acceptance_criteria: On an infeasible run, with AI disabled and no API key, the user sees how much specific rules must loosen to become satisfiable - sourced from a real backend solve, never fabricated. The existing XLSX/score/status contract is unchanged.

title: Investigate: instrumentation.subprocess.test.ts valid-config case fails EVEN serially (hardcoded port 34572 not serviceable)
description:
OBSERVED (2026-07-17, across multiple T12 M1 gate runs): the vitest 'standalone server config fail-fast (subprocess) > binds and becomes serviceable when config is valid' case (web/instrumentation.subprocess.test.ts:89) fails with 'expected false to be true' for outcome.becameServiceable on hardcoded PORT=34572. Consistent, not flaky. Full serial result: 1 failed | 53 passed | 1 skipped files; 1 failed | 662 passed | 17 skipped tests. Excluded from all T12 review verdicts as pre-existing infra.

WHAT THE TEST DOES: guarded by describe.skipIf(!hasBuild) where hasBuild = existsSync('.next/standalone/server.js'). So it only RUNS after a standalone build (e.g. after our 'rm -rf web/.next' fresh Playwright builds) — before a build it is SKIPPED, which is why it surfaces now. The valid case spawns the real standalone server (env BACKEND_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9, PUBLIC_ORIGIN=http://localhost:34572, PORT=34572), polls tryConnect(34572) every 200ms for 8s, and asserts it became connectable.

DISCREPANCY WITH nursing-sheduler-7go: 7go states this test 'passes serial / --no-file-parallelism' and attributes flake to DEFAULT-parallelism worker port contention. But here it fails EVEN under --no-file-parallelism (serial). So 7go's root-cause assumption does not fully hold in this environment; reconcile the two (this may be a second, distinct cause or 7go's serial-passes claim may be stale).

HYPOTHESES to check:
1. Hardcoded port 34572 is held/occupied by a long-running process in the Traycer/dev host (review agents' leading hypothesis) — but note: if a listener were ACCEPTING on 34572, tryConnect would succeed and the test would spuriously PASS; becameServiceable=false instead implies the spawned server never served (crashed/exited or a non-accepting occupant). Verify what actually holds 34572 (ss -ltnp | grep 34572) and whether the child exits early.
2. The spawned standalone server crashes on startup in this env for an unrelated reason (standalone artifact staleness after the rm -rf .next + rebuild dance; Node version; missing runtime env; next.config output:'standalone' assumptions) — capture child stdio (currently stdio:'ignore') and exitCode to see.
3. 8s timeout too short under a loaded host.
4. next.config output mode: confirm standalone output is actually produced/consistent with what the test spawns.

REPRO: rm -rf web/.next; build (Playwright webServer or next build) so .next/standalone/server.js exists; corepack pnpm -C web exec vitest run instrumentation.subprocess --no-file-parallelism.

FIX DIRECTION (likely shared with 7go): ephemeral/randomized port helper keeping PORT + PUBLIC_ORIGIN in sync; capture child stdio on failure; assert fail-fast behavior unchanged. Coordinate with / possibly supersede parts of nursing-sheduler-7go. Test-only; no product impact.

title: Consider: bare-duration (hours-only) shift authoring for contracted-hours accounting
description:
OPEN QUESTION / think-about item surfaced during T09 (People & Shift Types editors) cold re-review Major 7.

DL10-D4 settled that T09's working-time editor is clock-<select>-only (start/end + rest → auto-derived read-only duration); the design prototype overrides spec 03 FR-ED-06a for authoring, and T09 will NOT expose a bare-duration authoring mode. That is correct for ordinary FLOOR shifts, where the clock in/out + rest fully define the shift and the duration is a consequence.

BUT the core validator + producer schema DO accept a valid bare '{durationMinutes: N}' shape (clocks absent). The one place that shape is genuinely meaningful is HOURS-ONLY accounting toward contracted hours — e.g. a flexible/training/on-call block that contributes N hours toward a person's contracted-hours target without a fixed clock window. This is a T12 (Card editors + Contracted Hours, nursing-sheduler-qq0.12) / DL09 (minute-unit + working-time coefficients) concern, NOT a floor-shift working-time concern.

THINK ABOUT (defer decision to T12): Does the contracted-hours model need users to author duration-only shift types (no clocks)? If yes, where does that authoring live — a dedicated contracted-hours/coefficient surface (T12), NOT the T09 floor-shift working-time editor? If such shapes can arise from import/backend, T09 already preserves them on unrelated edits (DL10-D4 data-preservation guardrail) — confirm that guardrail is sufficient vs. needing real authoring.

No action now. Revisit when T12 is planned/implemented. Cross-refs: DL10-D4 (decision-logs/10-design-review-product-decisions), T09 cold-review Major 7, spec 03 FR-ED-06a, spec 12 contracted-hours, DL09.

title: Future: configurable / multi-type leave model (leave-configuration vision)
description:
Beyond-parity FUTURE vision, previously only a spec-level [DEFERRED] fence (spec 12 + DL05) — now tracked as a bead so it surfaces in bd. Currently NOT built; parity ships the single fixed-8h LEAVE day-state only. The vision, if pursued later:
- A top-level 'leaveTypes' container in the scenario schema + a backend 'creditMinutes' store (the backend today has NEITHER and extra="forbid" REJECTS leaveTypes — so this needs backend/contract work, not just UI).
- Configurable leave credit instead of the fixed 8h (LEAVE_CREDIT_MINUTES=480 frontend constant).
- Multiple / half-day leave types (e.g. Full-Day 8h + Half-Day 4h) + a Leave Types editor UI surface.
- Unit-toggle integer-safety for UNMARKED/generic shift counts (FR-CH-33 reconciliation) + hours semantics for unmarked generic counts.
Trigger to un-defer: a product decision to expand the leave model beyond the single fixed-8h type. Not calendar-driven.
design: Requires a NEW backend contract (leaveTypes container + creditMinutes store) BEFORE the frontend Leave Types editor is meaningful; backend currently rejects leaveTypes. Independent of beads cjr (roster) and t34 (AI). Rationale/fence lives in spec 12 (12-contracted-hours-and-leave) and DL05 (decision-logs/05-contracted-hours-and-leave-model). Kept as spec fences (NOT beaded): telemetry/ops non-goals, backlog nudges (raw-YAML guard channel, discovery nudge, bulk leave-calendar import, on-screen hours report), and t01 Home/App-Shell.
acceptance_criteria: A user can define multiple/configurable leave types (credit + optionally half-day) through a Leave Types editor, round-tripped through a backend that accepts leaveTypes; the fixed single-8h behavior remains the default.

title: Mobile person×date matrix — density strategy + touch paint (accepted-suboptimal, deferred)
description:
Design-completeness gap from the parity/feasibility review (findings 1-2). DECISION (2026-07-15): proceed with the current non-optimal design for the parity build; defer the improvement. Two issues on the Shift Requests person×date matrix — the handover's flagged KEY mobile challenge (handover section 8):

(1) Density = horizontal-scroll-only. The matrix answers ~100 people × ~31 days with a nested overflow:auto pane + sticky first column (shrink-a-table), not the progressive-disclosure / focused-row strategy the handover asked for. On a phone the 150px sticky nurse column eats ~40% of the viewport (~5-6 day cells visible); body scrolls ~3400px inside a 68vh pane; nested scroll fights page scroll. (ScreenRequests 90,94,523,536.)

(2) Quick-paint bulk entry is mouse-only (mousedown/mouseenter/global mouseup; no touch/pointer events) — the bulk-fill gesture is dead on touch, the priority device class. Single-cell tap-to-edit still works, so it degrades to one-cell-at-a-time. (ScreenRequests 347-350, 531-532.)

Revisit trigger: after the parity build ships / before any real mobile launch. Likely needs a design-track loop for a genuine mobile strategy (focused-row/progressive-disclosure view + touch-capable paint), not a mechanical patch.
design: Not a build-time patch — wants a real mobile matrix strategy from the design track (focused-row / progressive-disclosure view, virtualization, date-window paging) plus touch/pointer-event paint. Parity build proceeds with scroll-only + mouse paint as an accepted known limitation.
acceptance_criteria: The person×date matrix is usable on a phone for ~100 people × a month: bulk entry works on touch, and density is handled by a deliberate mobile strategy rather than horizontal scroll alone.

title: Post-parity: AI features (assist / conflict-fix)
description: Beyond-parity initiative from DL10 (design-review product decision D3). The design prototype includes an exploratory AI appendix (ScreenAppendixAI) plus an AI 'Planned' teaser that was removed from the committed Optimize flow. AI assist (e.g. reading an infeasible result and proposing targeted constraint fixes) has NO backend equivalent today and is out of the parity inventory (handover section 10). Build AFTER the roster-viewer initiative (roster takes higher priority). Tracked separately from the parity rebuild; must not block it.
design:
CORE FLOWS DRAFTED 2026-07-27. Artifacts under .traycer/epics/8b2235d5-8943-4f6d-a61e-3b671836217a/artifacts/ai-assistant/: index; decisions/ (20 settled, 12 rejected options, scope boundaries); flows/ (enablement-and-setup, panel-and-turn-lifecycle, guided-setup-conversation, tier-2-feasibility, privacy-and-data-boundary).

THIS SUPERSEDES THE ORIGINAL DESIGN NOTE ON THIS BEAD, which said 'needs its own backend/LLM contract designed first' and required it be 'wired to a real backend'. Both are now WRONG. The settled architecture is CLIENT-SIDE DIRECT: key stored in the browser, calls straight to the user's chosen provider, nothing through our backend. There is no backend contract to design and no backend AI work of any kind. See decision D17 and memory ai-features-optional-byo-key.

WHAT IT IS: a persistent dockable side panel on every screen, driving Guided AND Advanced. Off by default behind an AI toggle + provider + credential. No launcher at all while the toggle is off; unconfigured launcher only after opt-in.

LOAD-BEARING PREREQUISITE - the largest piece of work here and the one most likely to be underestimated: the app's invariants (ID uniqueness, reserved keywords, half-hour contracted grid, covering day-state exclusion) live in FORM COMPONENTS, and the store beneath performs no validation. An assistant writing to the store bypasses all of them. They must be lifted into a shared layer that forms call on Save and the assistant calls as a tool - one implementation, two ways in. This touches shipped, reviewed, well-tested editor code and is a PREREQUISITE for write access, not a follow-up.

SCOPE: Tier 2 ONLY. Tier-1 deterministic conflict checking is s30 (keyless, always on, ships first and independently). Elastic re-solve is l3m (keyless backend; serves the AI-off default user, which is why it is not behind the AI gate).

Sequencing unchanged: after cjr per DL10-D3, reaffirmed 2026-07-27.
acceptance_criteria: AI assist is available as a clearly-separated capability wired to a real backend, not fabricated; it is not required by any committed parity flow.
notes:
ASSUMPTIONS VERIFIED AGAINST CODE 2026-07-28. Four assumptions baked into the panel flow were checked; two needed correction.

1. STALE-DRAFT DISMISSAL - PARTLY WRONG AS WRITTEN. useCardEditorStaleGuard (card-editor-shell.tsx) is store-agnostic and PER-EDITOR: each caller supplies its own readLiveCards + onStale. It is not a global app property the assistant inherits. Widely implemented (5 card editors, contracted hours, groups-section, date-groups-card, people-table, shift-type-grid) BUT the Requests cell editor (cell-preference-editor.tsx) holds a draft and has NO stale guard - that is the silent-overwrite case today. Also the guard keys on ref-identity of the SPECIFIC slice the draft was formed against, so a write to a different slice that invalidates the draft may not trip it. Covering every draft-holding editor is work inside this initiative; needs an explicit inventory, not an assumption of universality.

2. NAVIGATION GUARD - CORRECT, with a condition and a gap. dispatchNavIntent() in shell/nav-guard-store.ts is module-level and documented as 'the single decision point every navigation surface (push, replace, browser Back, mode transitions) funnels through', so the assistant can use it. Condition: it only holds if the assistant routes through it - calling the Next router directly bypasses the guard exactly as a plain <Link> would. GAP: when a draft is open the guard stages a CONFIRM DIALOG, so assistant-initiated navigation pops a dialog the user did not trigger, with copy written for a user click. Recorded as open in the flow.

3. UNDO MID-TURN STOPS THE TURN - not an assumption about existing code, it is a design choice. Nothing contradicts it. Reclassified.

4. ABORTED TURN KEEPS WHAT LANDED, ONE UNDO - achievable but NOT free, and it exposes a tension the decision log did not acknowledge. zundo temporal is configured with limit 50 + partialize + equality and NO grouping/handleSet, so every tracked mutation is its own undo entry. The app's only existing collapse technique is stage-then-commit-once (commitPaintGesture folds a whole drag into one setReqData; loadScenario is one tracked full-slice setState). That technique is UNAVAILABLE here because D7 (apply immediately, watch it land) forbids withholding writes until turn end. So D7 + D8 together require new turn-scoped history machinery: suspend recording for the turn, deposit one pre-turn restore point when it settles. CRITICAL: the restore point must also be deposited on the ABORT path - if it only happens on clean completion, an aborted turn's applied changes are unreachable by undo entirely, worse than the flow promises.

Artifacts updated: flows/panel-and-turn-lifecycle (new 'Two things this depends on that do not exist yet' section + corrected interaction table + open nav-dialog copy item), decisions/index.md (D8 annotated with the D7 tension).
DESCRIPTIONS DECISION 2026-07-28 (D21/D22). Free-text descriptions are sent to the LLM UNMODIFIED, with no per-field disclosure. User directive: choosing a provider that respects privacy is the user's responsibility.

DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM THE OPTIMIZE PATH - document it, do not 'fix' it. web/lib/scenario/prepare-optimize-submission.ts recursively strips every free-text description on the anonymized path ('so no identifying prose leaves for a possibly third-party solver'). The AI path does NOT. Rationale for the asymmetry: the solver reads nothing from descriptions so stripping is free there; the assistant reads them constantly (often the only signal separating two structurally identical rules), so stripping would degrade the feature in exchange for a partial mitigation of a risk the user accepted when choosing a provider.

D22 - COPY CONSTRAINT, load-bearing: the Settings disclosure must read 'Staff and group IDs are replaced with placeholders', NOT 'Staff names'. Identifier substitution is what the system does; a claim about names becomes false the moment a name appears in a description. This is not a disclosure about descriptions - it is avoiding an inaccurate promise. Do not let copywriting 'improve' this back to 'names'.

VERIFIED THIS SESSION (sub-agent checks, cross-checked by me):
- Store performs zero validation; all four named invariants live in components (entity-editor/core/validation.ts, working-time.ts, coverings-model.ts). Confirms the initiative's largest work item.
- Three scenario-store mutation primitives confirmed.
- Optimize run state IS readable generically: hot-store runView (lifecycle, jobId, result, progress, log, error, controls).
- Draft DETECTION is global (hasLosableDrafts()); only DISMISSAL is per-editor.
- useUndoRedoShortcuts() calls temporal.undo() unconditionally with no pause awareness - active hazard during a suspended-history turn; the shortcut handler must be made turn-aware.
- No nested-pause protection; an interrupted turn cannot rely on synchronous cleanup to resume history recording.
- ~330 user actions: plausible (independent estimate bracketed 300-400), not exactly verifiable.
CRITIQUE TRIAGED + 3 DECISIONS SETTLED 2026-07-28. Full critique: artifacts/ai-assistant/reviews/core-flows-critique/index.md (5 blocking, 7 drift, 9 gaps).

NEW DECISIONS:
D23 - Turn undo reverses the assistant's OWN OPERATIONS, never a snapshot restore. Critical catch: the flow allows the user to edit during a turn, so a snapshot restore would silently revert their concurrent edits - data loss, not a UX wrinkle. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE TOOL LAYER: every assistant-callable action must be able to describe its own inverse. That is a design constraint on D14's shared action layer, not a retrofit. An action whose inverse cannot be expressed cannot be exposed to the assistant.
D24 - Nothing hints the assistant exists while the toggle is off, not even a dismissible contextual pointer. Accepted cost recorded: the feature is justified by newcomer onboarding, and a version reachable only by browsing Settings mostly reaches people who already know.
D25 - Undo is session-scoped; the change list is not. History never persists and clears on reload, so after a refresh the change list is a RECORD, not an offer to reverse. Do not render a dead Undo button on a restored transcript.
D9 REASON RESTATED - deletes are gated for BLAST RADIUS, not referent misresolution. The original reason applied equally to wide updates, which stay ungated because their effects are visible where they land. A cascade reaches preferences, matrix cells, group members and export rows at once and cannot be eyeballed afterwards.

ALSO FIXED FROM THE CRITIQUE:
- Privacy flow had an internal contradiction: two adjacent rows both required and disclaimed prose name-scanning. An id-map walk cannot reach free text, so 'user types a name -> it is pseudonymised' was unimplementable. Corrected, plus an explicit scope statement that pseudonymisation covers the STRUCTURED DOCUMENT only - chat text and descriptions travel unmodified.
- Tier-2 verification had no INCONCLUSIVE state. A solve that times out without proof is neither 'works' nor 'didn't help', and on a hard model it is the LIKELY outcome - reporting it as 'didn't help' would bury working fixes. Added, plus Verified-badge staleness on scenario change.
- Tier-2 verification solves contend for the single run slot the app already serialises with its own cleanup/recovery protocol. Recorded as open: refuse during an active run, queue, or share - and what the user sees. Risk if unhandled: a verification wedges the slot ordinary runs depend on.

PUSHED BACK ON: the critique called one-turn-one-undo 'not reachable'. Overstated - no mechanism EXISTS, which the flow already said. Its evidence (withPausedReplace wipes all history) shows the existing helper is wrong for this, not that the concept is broken.
FOUR DECISIONS 2026-07-28 (second critique round). RECORDED HERE FIRST because the ai-assistant artifact files have been reverting and losing edits - beads is the surviving record.

D28 - THE TURN IS EXCLUSIVE. While a turn runs the scenario is READ-ONLY: editing surfaces disabled, undo/redo unavailable. Chosen over allowing concurrent edits. WHY: each zundo entry is a whole-slice snapshot (partialize: pickScenario), so collapsing a turn into one entry means suspending recording and depositing one pre-turn restore point. If the user could edit in that window, undoing the turn would restore a state predating THEIR changes too. Blocking removes the failure mode at source.
  THIS REVERSES D23 (no-snapshot / inverse-operations) AND DISSOLVES ITS TOOL-LAYER CONSTRAINT: with editing blocked, a snapshot restore is safe, so actions no longer need to describe their own inverse. That also dissolves the critique's B3 finding (deleteEntity/renameEntity are lossy so an inverse cannot be derived) - no inverse is needed.
  D8 is now literally true: one history entry, ordinary undo shortcut reverses the turn.
  NON-NEGOTIABLE: (a) Cancel always available and always restores editability - a hung turn must never leave the app read-only; (b) the restore point MUST be deposited on the abort path too, else an aborted turn's changes are unreachable by undo; (c) if editing is ever unblocked, one-entry undo becomes unsafe and both must be revisited together - they are a package; (d) an open form draft at turn start must be resolved before the turn begins (dismiss or refuse) - OPEN which.
  ACCEPTED COST: the product is briefly modal; turns run for many seconds. Watching the change land still works (that is a read).
  HAZARDS VERIFIED: the undo keyboard shortcut is not turn-aware (calls undo unconditionally); nothing guards a second suspension; an interrupted turn cannot rely on synchronous cleanup to restore editability.

D26 REVISED - refusal defined against BACKEND EXECUTION CAPACITY ONLY. My earlier framing was wrong on two counts. (1) 'Sharing is impossible' - FALSE: docker/compose.yml says 'One Uvicorn worker initially... Redis makes multiple workers safe; worker count is a measured capacity setting, not a correctness requirement.' It is a tunable default, not an invariant. (2) 'Contention is rare' - depends which slot, and optimize-run-outcome explicitly forbids conflating the three. If it meant the browser's LOCAL RECOVERY SLOT, a check would be refused exactly when Tier 2 is reached, since an infeasible run holds that slot until Dismiss/cleanup - inverting the reasoning.
  SETTLED: a check is refused only while a solve is ACTUALLY EXECUTING. Never because of a retained server job record, never because of the local recovery slot. An infeasible run holds the recovery slot but occupies no worker, so Tier 2 is reachable.
  ALSO SETTLED (was unspecified, the damaging direction): 'Run again' is NEVER blocked by a check, and requesting a run cancels a pending check.

D29 - PSEUDONYMISATION DROPPED. Real people/group IDs are sent to the LLM. REVERSES D16. Rationale (consistent with D21): the user chooses the provider and is responsible for its privacy posture. Dissolves the critique's B5 finding that buildIdMap numbers P1/P2 positionally so adding or deleting a nurse renumbers everyone - a real bug for multi-turn chat where P7 could mean two different nurses across turns.
  CONSEQUENCE - D22 IS VOID AND ITS COPY MUST BE REMOVED, NOT NARROWED. The Settings line 'Staff and group IDs are replaced with placeholders' becomes wholly false. Remaining true disclosure: key is browser-local, requests go straight to the chosen provider, nothing through our servers. NO claim of name or ID protection may survive anywhere.
  Also removes the reverse-map display machinery and the 'mirrors what the app does for the solver' framing (which was false three ways anyway: the existing path uses peopleOnlyIdMap so group ids are untouched, it is a user toggle not a path property, and the solver is self-hosted).

D30 - CASCADING RENAMES ARE GATED like deletes. A rename rewrites references across preferences, matrix cells, group members, history and export rows - the same blast radius that justifies D9, and equally un-eyeballable. Closes the gap the critique found in D9's restated reason.
Handoff written. See plans/handoffs/HANDOFF_domain-ui-restoration_tier1-and-ai-planning_2026-07-28.md (chain domain-ui-restoration seq 2). Core flows + decision log D1-D30 complete, 2 critique rounds applied. NOTE: Traycer artifacts reverted mid-session; bead notes are canonical for D21-D30.
